news.title: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
news.title_en: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
news.author: Jess Weatherbed
news.article_content:
Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called “Visuals,” allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork.

Visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android. The exact layout differs across Suno’s desktop and mobile interfaces, but users will find a new Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. Web users can also access Visuals by selecting the three dot menu on a song in their library. From there, users can select which section of the track to use, up to a maximum of 15 seconds, and select a reference image to build the generated video clip.

There are three options available for the starting image reference: selecting one of the original character presets provided by Suno, uploading your own photo or artwork, or generating the image directly on Suno using descriptive prompts. The image generation capabilities also allow users to select specific aspect ratios, optimizing results for landscape or portrait modes and online platforms.

For video generation, users can select whether the reference image is used as the start or end frame, making it easier to edit the 15-second clips together. There’s a toggle to automatically lipsync vocals to the generated video, and tools for adjusting aspect ratio and clip length. Visuals also includes a dedicated video editing timeline for assembling clips into longer videos, and adding customizable song lyric text.

The H3 Move AI model is being used to power Visuals, based on H3 from MiniMax. Suno says the AI has been “optimized for our community including adding additional protections and safeguards,” which include a “suite of new text and visual filters” designed to block people from using or generating the likeness of specific artists, public figures, copyrighted works and IP. Visuals also uses its own “Visuals credits” to generate videos and images, which are distinct from the song credits used to make AI music, meaning Suno users will have additional expenses to pay in order to use this new feature.

The Visuals launch follows Suno introducing a Speech feature in October for generating spoken words and voiceovers. Adding video capabilities is another attempt to diversify the platform after Suno’s music generator attracted a number of high-profile lawsuits, though it seems some users would rather the company focus on improving those song-generating capabilities. In the YouTube video for the Visuals launch, one user says “FIX AUDIO BEFORE ADDING CRAP NOBODY ASKED FOR” — a sentiment that other commenters are echoing.

news.title_zh: Suno推出AI视频生成功能
news.summary_zh: Suno推出“Visuals”视觉生成工具，依托MiniMax模型支持音乐驱动的视频合成与唇形同步

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 音乐AI平台Suno上线“Visuals”视觉生成功能，利用MiniMax驱动的H3 Move模型，支持用户通过参考图片或提示词生成15秒AI视频，并具备自动唇形同步功能。该模块引入了独立于音乐积分的“Visuals积分”计费系统，并内置了针对艺术家版权及特定公众人物形象的过滤保护机制。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Suno has expanded its multimodal capabilities with 'Visuals,' a video generation tool powered by MiniMax’s H3 Move model. The feature enables users to generate 15-second music-synced video clips with automated lip-syncing, utilizing a separate credit-based system and enhanced safety filters to mitigate potential copyright and deepfake risks.

elements_zh.where: Suno全平台终端（网页、iOS、Android）
elements_zh.what: 上线Visuals视觉生成功能，支持视频合成与唇形同步，采用MiniMax H3模型
elements_zh.why: 在音乐生成业务之外进行商业模式多元化布局，应对版权质疑并增加用户ARPU值

elements_en.what: Launched 'Visuals' feature for music-driven video synthesis and lip-syncing via MiniMax H3
elements_en.why: Strategic business diversification and increasing monetization to counter copyright headwinds

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Suno通过多模态扩张，正试图从单一的音乐生成工具转型为闭环的内容生产生态。引入独立计费系统体现了其在面临高额版权诉讼压力下，亟需通过提升产品附加值与用户留存率来优化单位经济模型的意图，而内置安全过滤则是其应对监管审查的合规“防御工事”。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By expanding into multimodal generation, Suno aims to pivot from a niche music generator to a comprehensive content creation ecosystem. The introduction of a dedicated billing system reveals a strategic need to improve unit economics amid copyright litigation, while integrated safety filters signal an urgent move toward regulatory risk mitigation.

news.article_content_zh:
Suno 推出了图像和视频生成功能，这是其超越人工智能音乐平台的最新努力。这项名为“Visuals”的新功能允许用户将 Suno 歌曲转换为人工智能生成的视频剪辑，自动与歌词进行口型同步，或者通过提示描述制作可用作缩略图和专辑插图的图像。

视觉效果可在网络、iOS 和 Android 上使用。 Suno 的桌面和移动界面的确切布局有所不同，但用户会在每个版本的“创建”模式下找到一个新的“视觉效果”选项卡。 Web 用户还可以通过选择库中歌曲的三点菜单来访问视觉效果。从那里，用户可以选择要使用的轨道部分（最多 15 秒），并选择参考图像来构建生成的视频剪辑。

可用于起始图像参考的三个选项：选择 Suno 提供的原始字符预设之一、上传您自己的照片或艺术作品，或使用描述性提示直接在 Suno 上生成图像。图像生成功能还允许用户选择特定的宽高比，优化横向或纵向模式以及在线平台的结果。

对于视频生成，用户可以选择是否将参考图像用作开始帧或结束帧，从而更轻松地一起编辑 15 秒的剪辑。有一个开关可以自动将人声与生成的视频进行口型同步，还有用于调整宽高比和剪辑长度的工具。视觉效果还包括专用的视频编辑时间线，用于将剪辑组装成更长的视频，并添加可自定义的歌词文本。

H3 Move AI 模型基于 MiniMax 的 H3，用于为视觉效果提供支持。 Suno 表示，人工智能已经“针对我们的社区进行了优化，包括增加额外的保护和保障”，其中包括“一套新的文本和视觉过滤器”，旨在阻止人们使用或生成特定艺术家、公众人物、受版权保护的作品和知识产权的肖像。 Visuals还使用自己的“视觉学分”来生成视频和图像，这与用于制作AI音乐的歌曲学分不同，这意味着Suno用户将需要支付额外费用才能使用这一新功能。

Suno 在 10 月份推出了用于生成口语和画外音的语音功能，随后推出了视觉效果。在 Suno 的音乐生成器引发了一系列引人注目的诉讼之后，添加视频功能是平台多元化的又一尝试，尽管一些用户似乎更希望该公司专注于改进这些歌曲生成功能。在视频发布的 YouTube 视频中，一位用户说“在添加没人要求的垃圾之前先修复音频”——其他评论者也表达了同样的观点。

【起因与机理】在音乐生成业务之外进行商业模式多元化布局，应对版权质疑并增加用户ARPU值
【关键技术规格】基于MiniMax H3模型构建视觉生成工作流。
【各方立场与态度】建立独立视觉积分体系并强化艺术家版权保护机制。

[Key Technical Spec] Built on the MiniMax H3 model for visual generation workflows.

news.article_content:
Sony has confirmed that the recently released PS5 firmware 14.23 update is required to play GTA 6, in a social media post boosted by Rockstar Games.

Yesterday November 17, Sony released PS5 system software update 26.07-14.23.00, which weighed in at 1.267 GB. According to Sony’s official patch notes, it makes “some security fixes to the system software.”

Now, just hours before GTA 6 launches at midnight across the world, the PlayStation Support U.S. X / Twitter account confirmed what many had suspected: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.” The official Rockstar Games account then reposted it to its 23.7 million followers.

### Why has Sony issued this PS5 update warning?

It is believed this unprecedented PS5 update cuts PlayStation Network access to older firmware, which means if you haven’t upgraded to 14.23 you will not be able to play GTA 6 on PS5. 14.23 released just a day after a prominent PS5 hacker claimed to be the first person to have “dumped” a game binary at 14.22, although they did not share any jailbreak.

The PlayStation homebrew scene has made headlines in the last two months for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late September, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community because, at the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week were compatible with the jailbreak. This was of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy.

However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the more recent 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software. So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security.

This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak was made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.

Just last week, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, told IGN that the company was taking security seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

During an investor-focused Q&A, Zelnick was asked multiple times about this AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and some companies have even given staff bonus time off to play it. We've got plenty more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, including details on the New Zealand trick people are using to play early, Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research, and — finally — confirmation of the actress who plays Lucia.
news.article_content_zh:
在 Rockstar Games 推动的社交媒体帖子中，索尼确认需要更新最近发布的 PS5 固件 14.23 才能玩 GTA 6。

昨天11月17日，索尼发布了PS5系统软件更新26.07-14.23.00，大小为1.267GB。根据索尼官方补丁说明，它“对系统软件进行了一些安全修复”。

现在，就在《GTA 6》全球午夜发售前几个小时，PlayStation Support U.S. X / Twitter 账户证实了许多人的猜测：“索尼互动已经发布了玩《侠盗猎车手 VI》之前所需的 PS5 系统软件更新。玩家应该在 11 月 19 日午夜之前下载此更新，以便在 11 月 19 日发售当天做好玩游戏的准备。”随后，Rockstar Games 官方帐户将其转发给其 2370 万粉丝。

### 索尼为何发布PS5更新警告？

据信，这次史无前例的 PS5 更新会切断 PlayStation Network 对旧固件的访问，这意味着如果您尚未升级到 14.23，您将无法在 PS5 上玩 GTA 6。就在 14.23 发布的前一天，一位著名的 PS5 黑客声称是第一个在 14.22“转储”游戏二进制文件的人，尽管他们没有分享任何越狱信息。

过去两个月，PlayStation 自制程序因发布早期固件的 PS5 越狱而成为头条新闻。例如，9月底，支持所有运行固件7.00-13.60的PS5主机的越狱在自制软件社区引起了震动，因为当时这意味着上周未更新的所有PS5（包括PS5 Pro）都与越狱兼容。这对于索尼和 PS5 的安全具有重大意义，因为拥有越狱 PS5 的人可以修改他们的游戏机，从而可能为视频游戏盗版打开大门。

然而，我们发现一些 PS5 游戏随后需要更新的 14.00 固件才能下载更新，这引发了针对更新后的系统软件发布新越狱的新努力。因此，有一场打地鼠游戏正在上演，自制软件界正在努力为最新的 PS5 固件发布新的越狱，然后当索尼发布旨在增强安全性的新固件更新时，再次进行这一切。

这反过来又引发了人们的担忧，如果 PS5 越狱可用于 GTA 6 所需的固件，那么 Rockstar 的游戏可能会在 PS5 上被盗版，甚至可能在 PC 上提供。

索尼面临的问题是，它是否能够采取足够的措施，最终在自制游戏领域赢得这场打地鼠游戏。这对索尼来说是一场生存危机，发行商和开发商都依赖索尼来保证其 PlayStation 版本的安全。但随着强大的人工智能模型的出现，风险显着上升。

就在上周，Rockstar 母公司 Take-Two 的首席执行官斯特劳斯·泽尼克 (Strauss Zelnick) 告诉 IGN，该公司正在认真对待安全问题，并坚称粉丝们更愿意玩正式的《GTA 6》，而不是非官方的 PC 版本，因为它拥有 Rockstar 所希望的所有花哨功能。

在一次以投资者为中心的问答中，泽尔尼克多次被问及这个人工智能逆向工程问题。他再次做出了强硬的回应，暗示 Take-Two 已准备好请律师。

“由于文件大小、盗版的复杂性、与服务器的连接等因素，这项业务基本上永远不会受到盗版问题的影响，”他开始说道。 “毫无疑问，由于技术限制，要按照预期复制我们游戏的体验是非常困难的。

“也就是说，正如你所说，这将成为一个更大的挑战，我们也意识到了这一点。因此，我们完全专注于加强我们的技术防御并适当加强我们的法律活动。与此同时，毫不客气地说，现有的每一项娱乐业务都受到某种盗版因素的影响。因此，这可能会或多或少地侵入我们的业务。我认为这是可以管理的，我们会专注于它。”

《GTA 6》预计将成为有史以来规模最大的娱乐游戏，一些公司甚至为员工提供了玩这款游戏的奖金。在 GTA 6 于 11 月 19 日发布之前，我们已经获得了更多有关 GTA 6 的信息，包括人们早期玩的新西兰技巧的详细信息、Rockstar 现实生活中的侠盗猎车手研究前线的黑帮故事，以及最后确认扮演露西亚的女演员。

Keza MacDonaldWed 18 Nov 2026 06.00 ESTLast modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 06.03 ESTShare Prefer the Guardian on Google In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. There is such a multiplicity of things on offer here that it is difficult to nail down what this game definitively is. Is it an interactive crime movie? A city simulator? A driving game? A sort of absurdly expansive version of The Sims in which the people you’re dressing up and looking after just happen to be professional criminals? It will be different for everyone – that is the beauty of it.

For me, though, this game is about Jason and Lucia, the fugitive couple through whom you experience all that Leonida has to offer. Jason is muscular, handsome, ex-military, steady and unflappable, sincere but spare with words. Lucia has been boosting cars since the age of 14, has a wicked sense of humour and takes zero bullshit. (Lucia is the scarier one; I found myself turning much more quickly to violence when playing as her.) At the start, Lucia is incarcerated and Jason is making a go of things in the sunbeaten Keys, working for a dodgy guy down on the marina and renting a run-down house on stilts with a jetty round the back and a pet snake. When Lucia gets out of prison, the two of them try to make some kind of life for themselves – but before long they get caught up with the wrong people and have to flee the cosy life they’ve just started building.

For a long time you really are two-bit criminals on the run, getting in with every dirtbag petty thief and drug-runner you come across in order to scrape some cash together and stay under the radar. You meet hillbilly pill-heads and biker gangs, friendly conspiracy theorists, a shady doctor, Lucia’s former prison friends and their lowlife boyfriends. By the time I actually got to Vice City – a glitzy den of sin, the centre of all Leonida’s pleasures and all its most extravagant criminality, where the gangbangers hustle on social media and even the narcos are obsessed with their Instagram clout – I had been playing for 30 hours. It took me 70 hours to finish the game and I could have taken longer.

Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming, and outside the story missions you can do whatever you please. There are nightclubs, gyms, flea markets, malls, restaurants, clothes shops, basketball courts, shooting ranges, aircraft hangars, projects and mansions, places to hunt and fish or go kayaking, gas stations and thousands of individuals engaged in conversation as you pass by. Interesting things are always happening in your peripheral vision. You might witness the cops chasing someone down to plant drugs on them, or overhear an interesting confrontation, or see a car speeding away and wonder where it’s going – though interesting things always seemed to happen when I was driving a stolen car at high speed towards a discerning buyer, or otherwise unable to stop and follow my nose. Thankfully, another opportunity would always present itself.

r’s perfect simulation was me. All this detail and realism comes with some disadvantages, namely complex controls and a tendency for the game’s systems to collide with my intentions in unexpected and sometimes annoying ways. Here I am, driving at high speed through the city before clipping the kerb and flipping my car, causing a massive pile-up. Here I am pressing the wrong button and accidentally punching a random passerby rather than greeting them as intended, kicking off a ridiculous skirmish in which I have to knock out half the customers at a restaurant before running from the cops. Here I am again pressing the wrong button at a bike rack and ending up pinned beneath a tumbling row of bicycles. Missions can go south very quickly and for reasons that aren’t always obvious. In every street race I wiped out spectacularly by crashing into something I couldn’t properly see, while my opponents magically recovered from every collision and sped ahead. This can be a frustrating game at times: unpredictable, laborious, unwieldy and, occasionally, unfair. That is because you are not the master of the game world. You simply exist within it.

Like most compelling crime fiction, Jason and Lucia’s story involves an escalating series of messy events that pull them further and further from where they started, and have you constantly wondering how on earth they’re going to get out of the newest trouble they’re in. To avoid spoilers, substantive discussion of this story can only happen in the coming weeks. But I will say that I was rooting so hard for Jason and Lucia by the end that I felt quite sick with worry about what was going to happen to them, pacing back and forth in front of my TV throughout the final missions. Among all the expectations I had for GTA VI, I did not expect it to make me so emotional.

r – how she smiles fondly at him when they dance together, their playful banter, the stick-ups they pull off as a duo, their resilience and faith in themselves and each other in the face of escalating disaster – I found it impossible not to care for them. They are our avatars in GTA VI’s world but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim. It made me care about them much more. When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do.

This is indicative of a tonal shift for Grand Theft Auto that became more obvious the more I played. This series is famous for its violence, misanthropy and pitch-black humour. I have been invested in its characters before, have even rooted for some of them, but I have rarely liked them or related to them. This is the first GTA that wants to encourage some measure of empathy alongside its trademark violent chaos. I was astonished to discover that the game offers you small incentives for acts of kindness, such as texting your partner a selfie, doing your neighbour a favour or throwing your rubbish in the bin rather than dropping it on the ground. Jason and Lucia are not extravagant caricatures, but two people trying to make it in a world totally stacked against them. Pretty much everyone in this Floridian fever-dream is a total crook, on the take or mixed up in some bullshit scheme. It’s so easy to get away with crime in this city, and so difficult to do things the right way. The events of this game might be totally outlandish but these characters and their motivations keep things at least somewhat grounded.

s: how Grand Theft Auto conquered the music world Read moreIf you thought this newfound heart might tone down GTA’s 18-rated provocativeness, however, you would be very wrong. The protagonists may be surprisingly relatable but they exist in a world that is absurdly foul-mouthed, filthy and over-the-top offensive in every imaginable way. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating. Barely a half-hour ever goes by without someone snorting coke off a knife blade, or some full-frontal nudity. There are missions set inside a pornographer’s mansion and a small-town strip club; you can visit those clubs and get a private dance (as either Jason or Lucia, for what it’s worth, or together). At one point Lucia opens the wrong hotel room door to see a woman in a corset wielding a golf club, thwacking balls at a guy’s testicles. On the in-game TV there is a reality show about horny geriatrics. It does not so much push the boundaries of taste as ignore the existence of taste. It contains every perverted scenario you could imagine and several more that would never occur to you.

Sometimes it is a little jarring to emerge from a really pivotal and moving scene between Jason and Lucia into a virtual city where the billboards read things like “WANTED for shitting everywhere: THE SHIT BEAST.” But I found these two sides of GTA’s personality surprisingly easy to accommodate. It’s not as though the story is without its many moments of absurd levity and humour, too: at one point I was taking a bunch of terrifying gang leaders with face tattoos on a real-estate tour, where they sincerely admired the outdoor space with brick pizza oven, and another time I was chasing a man wearing nothing but an alligator thong through a well-to-do suburban neighbourhood. A game this huge can accommodate both pathos and lewdness, and much more.

a – Grand Theft Auto’s first female protagonist – changed how a lot of this landed for me. GTA has never been particularly kind to women (or men, for that fact, but in past games it has exclusively been the women who were sexualised). There is still a lot of sexism in GTA VI’s world, but now we have Lucia to react to it. This is the first GTA in which I have felt the women are treated as people, not only Lucia but also the many other female characters in the story, from up-and-coming rappers to Lucia’s mother, from a jaded strip-club worker to a badass middle-aged drug-runner whose custom purple carbine rifle is her prized possession. This is a game in which women can be as violent, visibly tough and deeply messed-up as the men. And without wanting to give too much away: there are male strippers in Leonida, too.

I am not about to make a case for GTA VI as a feminist game – there is much to be offended by here, if you are so inclined – but I will say that as a woman who has played and enjoyed every GTA game while also often rolling my eyes at their casual sniggering misogyny, GTA VI hits different for me. I liked it more because the women aren’t always the butt of a joke. Also for the first time, I did not find the violence gratuitous or overblown, despite the fact that this is a story about crime and criminals. There is nothing here like GTA V’s infamous torture mission, which made me feel sick. It says a lot that of all the immoral opportunities afforded to me in Vice City, the only thing I straight-up said “no” to was getting involved in a metaverse scam. THAT would be going too far.

t’s possible to sum up a game as vast as this, and the closest I come is the nightclubs. These show GTA VI at its most extravagant: hundreds of virtual people under the pulsing lights, all dressed up to go out, dancing to a fastidiously curated soundtrack featuring some of the real world’s most famous artists as the controller pulses to the bassline in your hands. These big nights out are an opportunity for both Vice City’s sleaziest denizens and Rockstar’s developers to flash their cash: they are the game’s most ostentatiously expensive and showy scenarios. But at the centre of it all, there are Jason and Lucia, dancing together, focused on each other in the midst of all this chaos and excess.

Keza is one of the first people to have played GTA VI. Ask her anything in our live Q&A at 4pm today. Join here.

Grand Theft Auto VI is out 19 November; £69.99 / €79.99 / A$159.95 / $79.99

This is a game in which women can be as violent, visibly tough and deeply messed-up as the men. And without wanting to give too much away: there are male strippers in Leonida, too.

I am not about to make a case for GTA VI as a feminist game – there is much to be offended by here, if you are so inclined – but I will say that as a woman who has played and enjoyed every GTA game while also often rolling my eyes at their casual sniggering misogyny, GTA VI hits different for me. I liked it more because the women aren’t always the butt of a joke. Also for the first time, I did not find the violence gratuitous or overblown, despite the fact that this is a story about crime and criminals. There is nothing here like GTA V’s infamous torture mission, which made me feel sick. It says a lot that of all the immoral opportunities afforded to me in Vice City, the only thing I straight-up said “no” to was getting involved in a metaverse scam. THAT would be going too far.

t’s possible to sum up a game as vast as this, and the closest I come is the nightclubs. These show GTA VI at its most extravagant: hundreds of virtual people under the pulsing lights, all dressed up to go out, dancing to a fastidiously curated soundtrack featuring some of the real world’s most famous artists as the controller pulses to the bassline in your hands. These big nights out are an opportunity for both Vice City’s sleaziest denizens and Rockstar’s developers to flash their cash: they are the game’s most ostentatiously expensive and showy scenarios. But at the centre of it all, there are Jason and Lucia, dancing together, focused on each other in the midst of all this chaos and excess.

Keza is one of the first people to have played GTA VI. Ask her anything in our live Q&A at 4pm today. Join here.

Grand Theft Auto VI is out 19 November; £69.99 / €79.99 / A$159.95 / $79.99

女性可以像男性一样暴力、明显强硬、一团糟……《侠盗猎车手 6》中的杰森和露西亚。照片：Rockstar Games 以全屏查看图片 女性可以像男性一样暴力、明显强硬且一团糟……《侠盗猎车手 6》中的杰森和露西亚。照片：Rockstar Games Review《侠盗猎车手 VI》评论 - 游戏中最堕落的世界现在也是其最伟大的爱情故事这款庞大的游戏具有令人难以置信的现实主义，很容易适应其标志性的脏话、OTT混乱 - 以及对中心逃亡夫妇的新同情

Keza MacDonaldWed 2026 年 11 月 18 日 06.00 ESTLast 修改于 2026 年 11 月 18 日星期三 06.03 ESTShare 更喜欢 Google 上的卫报 在 GTA VI 中，Rockstar 创造了我们所见过的最非凡、最细致的虚拟世界。回顾它感觉有点像尝试回顾巴黎：它包含如此多的潜在体验，以至于很难知道从哪里开始。如果你在过去几周里一直在监视我玩这款游戏，你很可能会发现我抢劫银行、射击杂草农场或在日落时分在高速公路上撕扯，并在游戏中的收音机中播放着《坏兔子》，但你也可能会发现我在健身房做深蹲、购物、组装咖啡桌或沿着海滩散步吃冰淇淋。这里提供的东西如此之多，以至于很难确定这款游戏到底是什么。这是一部互动犯罪电影吗？城市模拟器？驾驶游戏？某种荒诞的扩张版《模拟人生》，其中你所打扮和照顾的人恰好是职业罪犯？每个人的情况都会有所不同——这就是它的美妙之处。

但对我来说，这款游戏是关于杰森和露西亚这对逃亡夫妇的，通过他们你可以体验列奥尼达所提供的一切。杰森肌肉发达、英俊、退伍军人、沉着冷静、真诚但寡言少语。 Lucia 从 14 岁起就开始推销汽车，她有一种邪恶的幽默感，不接受任何废话。 （露西亚是更可怕的一个；我发现自己在扮演她时更快地转向暴力。）一开始，露西亚被监禁，杰森在阳光普照的群岛上做事，为码头上一个狡猾的家伙工作，租了一间破旧的高跷房子，后面有一个码头，还有一条宠物蛇。当露西娅出狱后，两人试图为自己创造某种生活，但不久他们就遇到了错误的人，不得不逃离他们刚刚开始建立的舒适生活。

在很长一段时间里，你实际上都是在逃的两位罪犯，与你遇到的每一个小偷和毒贩混在一起，以便凑到一些钱并保持在雷达之下。你会遇到乡巴佬、药丸头和摩托帮、友好的阴谋论者、阴暗的医生、露西娅的前监狱朋友和他们的下流男友。当我真正到达罪恶都市时——一个光鲜亮丽的罪恶巢穴，列奥尼达所有快乐和最奢侈犯罪的中心，黑帮分子在社交媒体上忙碌，甚至毒枭也沉迷于他们的 Instagram 影响力——我已经玩了 30 个小时。我花了 70 个小时才完成这个游戏，我本来可以花更长时间。

列奥尼达是如此栩栩如生，有时令人难以置信，如此巨大以至于让人感到不知所措，在故事任务之外你可以做任何你想做的事。这里有夜总会、健身房、跳蚤市场、商场、餐馆、服装店、篮球场、射击场、飞机库、项目和豪宅、打猎、钓鱼或划皮划艇的地方、加油站，以及成千上万的人在你经过时进行交谈。有趣的事情总是在你的余光中发生。你可能会目睹警察追捕某人并在他们身上放置毒品，或者无意中听到一场有趣的对抗，或者看到一辆汽车飞驰而去，想知道它要去哪里——尽管当我驾驶一辆偷来的汽车高速驶向一位挑剔的买家，或者无法停下来跟随我的鼻子时，有趣的事情似乎总是会发生。值得庆幸的是，另一个机会总会出现。

和大多数引人入胜的犯罪小说一样，杰森和露西亚的故事涉及一系列不断升级的混乱事件，这些事件使他们离起点越来越远，让你不断地想知道他们到底将如何摆脱他们所陷入的最新麻烦。为了避免剧透，对这个故事的实质性讨论只能在未来几周内进行。但我要说的是，到最后我非常支持杰森和露西亚，以至于我对他们会发生什么感到非常担心，在整个最后的任务中在电视前来回踱步。在我对 GTA VI 的所有期待中，我没想到它让我如此激动。

在这座城市里，犯罪很容易逃脱……《侠盗猎车手 VI》中的列奥尼达·凯斯 (Leonida Keys)。照片：Rockstar Games 这其中的关键是你与 Jason 和 Lucia 建立的联系。在他们陪伴了数十个小时之后，看着他们在一起——当他们一起跳舞时，她如何深情地对他微笑，他们顽皮的玩笑，他们作为二人组的表演，他们在面对不断升级的灾难时对自己和彼此的坚韧和信心——我发现不可能不关心他们。他们是我们在 GTA VI 世界中的化身，但他们并不是玩家的空白替身：你可以决定他们的行为，但不能决定他们的个性。他们感觉就像是真实的人，而不是随你的心血来潮跳舞的木偶。这让我更加关心他们。当这个故事让我有机会决定接下来会发生什么时，我想到的是他们会做什么，而不是我会做什么。

这表明《侠盗猎车手》的色调转变随着我玩得越多而变得越明显。该剧以其暴力、厌世和黑色幽默而闻名。我以前对它的角色很投入，甚至支持其中的一些角色，但我很少喜欢他们或与他们产生联系。这是第一部想要在其标志性的暴力混乱的同时鼓励一定程度的同理心的侠盗猎车手。我惊讶地发现，这款游戏为你的善行提供了一些小奖励，比如给你的伴侣发一张自拍照、帮邻居一个忙，或者把垃圾扔进垃圾桶而不是扔在地上。杰森和露西亚并不是夸张的漫画，而是两个人试图在一个完全反对他们的世界中生存的人。在这个佛罗里达狂热梦想中，几乎每个人都是彻头彻尾的骗子，要么上当受骗，要么卷入一些狗屎计划。在这座城市里，犯罪很容易逃脱惩罚，但以正确的方式做事却很难。这款游戏的事件可能完全古怪，但这些角色和他们的动机至少让事情有一定的基础。

有时，从杰森和露西娅之间真正关键且感人的场景进入虚拟城市会有点不和谐，那里的广告牌上写着“到处拉屎的通缉犯：狗屎野兽”。但我发现 GTA 性格的这两方面出奇地容易适应。这个故事也并非没有许多荒谬的轻浮和幽默的时刻：有一次，我带着一群可怕的、脸上有纹身的帮派头目去房地产参观，他们真诚地欣赏着带有砖砌披萨烤箱的户外空间；还有一次，我在一个富裕的郊区追逐一个只穿着鳄鱼丁字裤的男人。如此庞大的游戏可以容纳悲情和淫秽，甚至更多。

我并不打算将《GTA VI》视为一款女权主义游戏——如果你愿意的话，这里有很多值得冒犯的地方——但我想说的是，作为一个玩过并享受每一款《GTA》游戏的女性，同时也经常对她们随意窃笑的厌女症翻白眼，《GTA VI》对我来说是不同的。我更喜欢它，因为女人并不总是成为笑柄。同样是第一次，我没有发现暴力是无端的或夸大的，尽管事实上这是一个关于犯罪和罪犯的故事。这里没有什么比《GTA V》臭名昭著的酷刑任务更让我感到恶心的了。这充分说明了在罪恶都市为我提供的所有不道德机会中，我唯一直接说“不”的就是卷入虚拟宇宙骗局。那太过分了。

全屏查看游戏中最昂贵、最华丽的场景……《侠盗猎车手 VI》中的夜总会。照片：Rockstar Games 我一直在寻找能够概括《GTA VI》的东西，尽可能地概括如此庞大的游戏，而我最接近的就是夜总会。这些展示了《GTA VI》最奢华的一面：数百个虚拟人物在脉动的灯光下，都盛装外出，伴随着精心策划的配乐起舞，配乐中有一些现实世界最著名的艺术家，控制器随着您手中的低音线脉动。这些盛大的夜晚对于罪恶都市最肮脏的居民和 Rockstar 的开发者来说都是一个炫耀现金的机会：它们是游戏中最昂贵和最华丽的场景。但在这一切的中心，有杰森和露西娅，他们一起跳舞，在这一切混乱和过度的环境中专注于彼此。

news.author: Ellesheva Kissin
news.content_snippet:

news.summary_en: KPMG UK conducted its first end-to-end AI audit on a FTSE 250 firm, deploying over 100 AI agents under 'Project Exponential' to execute data collection and analysis. While AI demonstrated superior query depth compared to human auditors, the experiment revealed persistent limitations in regulatory mapping requiring human intervention.
news.article_content_en:
KPMG has carried out its first AI-based audit of a UK-listed company, saying the technology asked better questions than its own accountants about aspects of its client’s finances and dug deeper into some issues.

The Big Four firm this year deployed more than 100 AI agents to review the financial statements of an unnamed FTSE 250 company, running the experiment parallel to a conventional audit by its accountants.

In several cases “the AI was able to go so much deeper” than the regular audit team, said Cath Burnet, KPMG’s UK head of audit, adding that in some situations it had asked “better questions”.

But in one area of the audit, a human had to intervene after an AI agent failed to match a set of regulations to the company’s documents, she added.

The project underlines AI’s potential to disrupt the sector by allowing accounts to be checked more quickly and cheaply even as regulators raise concerns about the risks associated with relying on artificial intelligence.

Audit firms have traditionally billed clients for large teams of junior accountants doing labour-intensive work, supervised by a small number of senior staff.

KPMG acknowledged there were “clear time-saving opportunities” from AI-based audits but declined to say whether this would in turn reduce fees.

KPMG International has itself negotiated lower fees from its auditor by arguing that AI will make the work cheaper.

Rival Big Four accounting firm PwC has also run several “parallel audit” projects to test AI extensively without relying on it, said Andy Hammond, the firm’s global assurance leader.

Auditors had previously used AI to help perform specific audit tasks, but until now the technology had not been used across all phases of a large UK audit.

In KPMG’s experiment, codenamed Project Exponential, agents deployed on different parts of the audit worked autonomously with each other and were able to suggest next steps.

AI agents had gathered data and analysed and documented it before forming draft conclusions and observations for the audit.

A team built the agents in four months and then had an audit partner “sign off” the experimental audit, which was not relied on by KPMG when it formally signed off on the company’s accounts.

KPMG declined to disclose the exact size of the team used in its AI-based audit but said that two partners and one director had worked with senior managers and junior staff building and running the agents.

The Project Exponential team had a “different shape and size” to a traditional audit, Burnet said, but human involvement had remained “critical”.

Staff set the agents’ objectives, supplied information about the company’s business and previous audits, checked the agents’ work periodically and challenged their conclusions before finalising the audit opinion.

The project will be expanded to up to 20 larger audits and KPMG hopes to eventually offer AI-based audits to its clients.

But the required technology was not yet available at the scale needed to run thousands of audits, Burnet said. Some companies may prefer not to use the service, and few currently had “clean” enough data for AI agents to work with, she added.

The rapid adoption of AI has sparked concerns about whether auditors can adequately oversee work carried out by machines.

The UK accounting regulator, the Financial Reporting Council, warned this week that using AI could pose a “distinct threat” to auditors’ integrity and independence if they used insights from AI agents to advise their clients. Auditors are restricted from providing advisory services to audit clients.

“Whatever technology a firm uses, the auditor remains accountable,” said Mark Babington, executive director of regulatory standards at the FRC. “Auditors need to be able to explain how they used it, challenge its outputs and stand behind the evidence.”

A report from the Centre for Public Interest Audit, a policy and research group for large audit firms, found last month that 23 per cent of company audit committee chairs, who appoint and oversee auditors, had “limited” confidence in AI.

Concerns included the risk of auditors becoming over-reliant on AI, weakening their scepticism, as well as data security and potential “hallucinations”, where the technology gives false, misleading or fabricated information.

Burnet said KPMG’s system provided “full visibility and full traceability” of the AI agents’ work, recording their interactions with documents down to individual characters and timestamps. KPMG gave the FRC a high-level overview of its experiment.

【起因与机理】旨在验证AI在提升审计效率、挖掘财务异常方面的潜力，寻求降低劳动力密集型审计成本的路径

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To test potential for efficiency gains and cost reduction in labor-intensive auditing processes.
[Key Technical Spec] KPMG launched 'Project Exponential', utilizing 100+ AI agents for parallel audit testing.
[Key Position & Outlook] The industry is currently in an early validation phase, struggling to balance cost reduction with rigorous compliance.
news.article_content:
KPMG has carried out its first AI-based audit of a UK-listed company, saying the technology asked better questions than its own accountants about aspects of its client’s finances and dug deeper into some issues.

The Big Four firm this year deployed more than 100 AI agents to review the financial statements of an unnamed FTSE 250 company, running the experiment parallel to a conventional audit by its accountants.

In several cases “the AI was able to go so much deeper” than the regular audit team, said Cath Burnet, KPMG’s UK head of audit, adding that in some situations it had asked “better questions”.

But in one area of the audit, a human had to intervene after an AI agent failed to match a set of regulations to the company’s documents, she added.

The project underlines AI’s potential to disrupt the sector by allowing accounts to be checked more quickly and cheaply even as regulators raise concerns about the risks associated with relying on artificial intelligence.

Audit firms have traditionally billed clients for large teams of junior accountants doing labour-intensive work, supervised by a small number of senior staff.

KPMG acknowledged there were “clear time-saving opportunities” from AI-based audits but declined to say whether this would in turn reduce fees.

KPMG International has itself negotiated lower fees from its auditor by arguing that AI will make the work cheaper.

Rival Big Four accounting firm PwC has also run several “parallel audit” projects to test AI extensively without relying on it, said Andy Hammond, the firm’s global assurance leader.

Auditors had previously used AI to help perform specific audit tasks, but until now the technology had not been used across all phases of a large UK audit.

In KPMG’s experiment, codenamed Project Exponential, agents deployed on different parts of the audit worked autonomously with each other and were able to suggest next steps.

AI agents had gathered data and analysed and documented it before forming draft conclusions and observations for the audit.

A team built the agents in four months and then had an audit partner “sign off” the experimental audit, which was not relied on by KPMG when it formally signed off on the company’s accounts.

KPMG declined to disclose the exact size of the team used in its AI-based audit but said that two partners and one director had worked with senior managers and junior staff building and running the agents.

The Project Exponential team had a “different shape and size” to a traditional audit, Burnet said, but human involvement had remained “critical”.

Staff set the agents’ objectives, supplied information about the company’s business and previous audits, checked the agents’ work periodically and challenged their conclusions before finalising the audit opinion.

The project will be expanded to up to 20 larger audits and KPMG hopes to eventually offer AI-based audits to its clients.

But the required technology was not yet available at the scale needed to run thousands of audits, Burnet said. Some companies may prefer not to use the service, and few currently had “clean” enough data for AI agents to work with, she added.

The rapid adoption of AI has sparked concerns about whether auditors can adequately oversee work carried out by machines.

The UK accounting regulator, the Financial Reporting Council, warned this week that using AI could pose a “distinct threat” to auditors’ integrity and independence if they used insights from AI agents to advise their clients. Auditors are restricted from providing advisory services to audit clients.

“Whatever technology a firm uses, the auditor remains accountable,” said Mark Babington, executive director of regulatory standards at the FRC. “Auditors need to be able to explain how they used it, challenge its outputs and stand behind the evidence.”

A report from the Centre for Public Interest Audit, a policy and research group for large audit firms, found last month that 23 per cent of company audit committee chairs, who appoint and oversee auditors, had “limited” confidence in AI.

Concerns included the risk of auditors becoming over-reliant on AI, weakening their scepticism, as well as data security and potential “hallucinations”, where the technology gives false, misleading or fabricated information.

Burnet said KPMG’s system provided “full visibility and full traceability” of the AI agents’ work, recording their interactions with documents down to individual characters and timestamps. KPMG gave the FRC a high-level overview of its experiment.
news.article_content_zh:
毕马威对一家英国上市公司进行了首次基于人工智能的审计，称该技术比其自己的会计师对客户财务方面提出了更好的问题，并更深入地研究了一些问题。

这家四大公司今年部署了 100 多名人工智能代理来审查一家未具名的 FTSE 250 公司的财务报表，该实验与会计师进行的传统审计并行进行。

毕马威英国审计主管 Cath Burnet 表示，在某些情况下，“人工智能能够比常规审计团队深入得多”，并补充说，在某些情况下，它提出了“更好的问题”。

但她补充说，在审计的一个领域，由于人工智能代理未能将一系列规定与公司文件相匹配，因此必须由人类进行干预。

该项目强调了人工智能通过允许更快、更便宜地检查账户来颠覆该行业的潜力，尽管监管机构对依赖人工智能相关的风险表示担忧。

审计公司传统上向客户收取大量初级会计师团队的费用，这些初级会计师团队从事劳动密集型工作，并由少数高级员工监督。

毕马威承认基于人工智能的审计有“明显的节省时间的机会”，但拒绝透露这是否会反过来降低费用。

毕马威国际 (KPMG International) 本身已与审计师协商降低费用，理由是人工智能将使工作成本降低。

竞争对手四大会计师事务所普华永道也运行了多个“并行审计”项目，以在不依赖人工智能的情况下广泛测试人工智能，该公司全球审计负责人安迪·哈蒙德(Andy Hammond)表示。

审计人员此前曾使用人工智能来帮助执行特定审计任务，但到目前为止，该技术尚未在英国大型审计的所有阶段中使用。

在毕马威的实验中，代号为“指数计划”的实验中，部署在审计不同部分的代理相互自主协作，并能够提出后续步骤的建议。

人工智能代理收集数据并进行分析和记录，然后形成审计结论和意见草案。

一个团队在四个月内建立了代理，然后让审计合作伙伴“签署”了实验性审计，毕马威在正式签署公司账目时并没有依赖这一点。

毕马威拒绝透露其基于人工智能的审计所使用的团队的具体规模，但表示两名合伙人和一名董事与高级管理人员和初级员工一起构建和运营代理。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 毕马威在英国对一家富时250指数成分股公司实施了首次全流程AI审计实验，通过部署百余个AI代理进行数据抓取、分析与初步结论生成。该项目名为“指数化项目（Project Exponential）”，在与传统人工审计并行测试中，AI在逻辑质询深度上超越人类，但在法规匹配等复杂合规场景中仍需人工干预。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: KPMG UK conducted its first end-to-end AI audit on a FTSE 250 firm, deploying over 100 AI agents under 'Project Exponential' to execute data collection and analysis. While AI demonstrated superior query depth compared to human auditors, the experiment revealed persistent limitations in regulatory mapping requiring human intervention.

Amid mounting competition from Alibaba and ByteDance, co-founder Pony Ma is driving an aggressive internal AI shift, launching the Hy4 model; however, the company faces external headwinds from US restrictions on Chinese access to Southeast Asian data centers for AI training.

The country's social media leader reported revenue rose 8% to 207.3 billion yuan ($31.1 billion) in the September quarter, lower than the average analyst projection. Net income barely grew during the period.

The tepid results raise questions about billionaire co-founder Pony Ma's efforts to close the gap with longtime rivals Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (BABA) and ByteDance Ltd. in the AI era. Last week, he called on half of Tencent's 100,000-strong workforce to harness artificial intelligence in search of new growth avenues, while urging the rest try to boost efficiency in its gaming and social media businesses.

Tencent has claimed a spate of early successes in its AI push, releasing an Hy4 model this month that it said ranks among China's most powerful. Its WorkBuddy office tool claimed 32 million monthly active users in September, more than its direct rivals combined. At the helm of those efforts is Dowson Tong, one of Ma's key lieutenants, who is driving teams to experiment with products.

Ma slammed Tencent's AI endeavor as "a leaky ship" in May, then gathered employees at a company anniversary celebration this month where he urged them to contribute more. "If you don't embrace the ongoing intelligence revolution, you get disrupted. This is a matter of life and death," Ma said, according to a transcript of his remarks published by Tencent.

Competition in China's AI arena is only set to intensify with ByteDance preparing to launch a personal AI assistant and Alibaba planning to spin off its chip unit via an IPO in Hong Kong. Complicating matters, Washington this week unveiled new rules aimed at cutting off Chinese access to Southeast Asian data centers, disrupting a vital avenue for training and developing AI.

Much of Tencent's hopes now rest on WeChat, the ubiquitous app that's already shouldering much of the monetization burden in areas from advertising to live shopping. WeChat's native agent, Xiaowei, has been in testing since summer. Executives hope it will morph into an AI-first ecosystem that is central to the everyday lives of more than a billion people.

Chinese big tech firms have shifted toward building out AI data centers and stocking up on scarce chips even as investors increasingly scrutinize the near-term payoffs of such endeavors.

Tencent's free cash flow turned negative in the June quarter after it hiked capital spending by 180% to $8 billion. That's still on the conservative side compared with Silicon Valley giants like Meta Platforms Inc. and Microsoft Corp.

Funding a big portion of that spending is Tencent's mainstay games business. The company has become more cautious about starting projects anew during a global industry downturn, while turning to what it calls "evergreen" titles such as Honor of Kings to reap consistent profits.

In global markets, Path of Exile 2 from a New Zealand studio owned by Tencent is scheduled for a full launch in December after an initial rollout two years ago.

We don't expect Tencent to generate significant external sales from AI this year, given the monetization challenges in China's fragmented AI sector. The company's AI product lineup — concentrated in office tools, large-language models and coding assistants — isn't sufficiently differentiated from Alibaba and ByteDance, though it should benefit from internal synergies

--With assistance from Vlad Savov, Luz Ding, Henry Ren and Ville Heiskanen.

这家中国社交媒体领军企业报告称，9 月份所在季度的收入增长 8%，达到 2073 亿元人民币（合 311 亿美元），低于分析师的平均预测。在此期间净利润几乎没有增长。

不温不火的业绩引发了人们对亿万富翁联合创始人马化腾在人工智能时代缩小与长期竞争对手阿里巴巴集团控股有限公司（BABA）和字节跳动有限公司差距的努力的质疑。上周，他呼吁腾讯10万名员工中的一半利用人工智能寻找新的增长途径，同时敦促其余员工努力提高游戏和社交媒体业务的效率。

腾讯声称其人工智能推广取得了一系列早期成功，本月发布了一款 Hy4 模型，据称该模型跻身中国最强大的模型之列。其 WorkBuddy 办公工具 9 月份的月活跃用户数为 3200 万，超过其直接竞争对手的总和。领导这些工作的是马云的主要副手之一汤道森（Dowson Tong），他正在推动团队进行产品试验。

五月份，马云抨击腾讯的人工智能事业是“一艘漏水的船”，然后在本月的公司周年庆典上召集员工，敦促他们做出更多贡献。根据腾讯发布的讲话记录，马云表示：“如果你不接受正在进行的情报革命，你就会受到干扰。这是生死攸关的问题。”

随着字节跳动准备推出个人人工智能助理，阿里巴巴计划通过在香港 IPO 剥离其芯片部门，中国人工智能领域的竞争只会加剧。让事情变得更加复杂的是，华盛顿本周公布了新规则，旨在切断中国对东南亚数据中心的访问，扰乱培训和开发人工智能的重要途径。

腾讯现在的大部分希望寄托在微信上，这款无处不在的应用程序已经承担了从广告到直播购物等领域的大部分盈利负担。微信的原生代理小微自夏天以来一直在进行测试。高管们希望它将演变成一个人工智能优先的生态系统，成为超过十亿人日常生活的核心。

中国大型科技公司已转向建设人工智能数据中心并储备稀缺芯片，尽管投资者越来越关注此类努力的近期回报。

腾讯将资本支出增加 180% 至 80 亿美元后，第二季度的自由现金流转为负值。与 Meta Platforms Inc. 和微软公司等硅谷巨头相比，这仍然偏保守。

其中很大一部分支出是腾讯的支柱游戏业务提供的。在全球行业低迷时期，该公司对重新启动项目变得更加谨慎，同时转向《王者荣耀》等所谓的“常青”游戏，以获得持续的利润。

在全球市场，腾讯旗下新西兰工作室的《流放之路 2》在两年前首次推出后，计划于 12 月全面推出。

paragraphs: AI music generator Suno can now create images and video clips to go with its songs, thanks to a new feature called Visuals. The feature runs on H3 Move, a customized and safety-filtered version of MiniMax's video model H3. The clips run up to 15 seconds, follow the song's structure, pick up on lyrics, and support lip sync.

Users can start from a reference photo, a prompt, or one of Suno's preset characters. Lyric videos let you tweak fonts and colors, extend clips on a timeline, and pick the length and aspect ratio. Two quality tiers are available, "Fast"and "Standard."Filters block prompts and uploads that reference specific artists, celebrities, or copyrighted works. Before sharing content outside Suno, the platform adds an embedded watermark.
Visuals works on the web, iOS, and Android, and requires its own credits. Pro and Premier subscribers get a temporary allotment to try it out.

In late July, the Munich Regional Court I ruled against Suno in a lawsuit filed by GEMA, Germany's music rights organization, finding copyright infringement. Shortly after, Suno announced tools to label Suno-made songs as AI-generated on other platforms. The company has reached a deal with Warner Music, but Universal and Sony are still pursuing litigation.

news.article_content_zh:
得益于一项名为 Visuals 的新功能，AI 音乐生成器 Suno 现在可以创建与其歌曲相匹配的图像和视频剪辑。该功能在 H3 Move 上运行，H3 Move 是 MiniMax 视频模型 H3 的定制和安全过滤版本。这些剪辑长达 15 秒，遵循歌曲的结构，拾取歌词，并支持口型同步。

用户可以从参考照片、提示或 Suno 的预设角色之一开始。抒情视频可让您调整字体和颜色、在时间轴上扩展剪辑以及选择长度和纵横比。有两个质量等级可供选择：“快速”和“标准”。过滤器会阻止引用特定艺术家、名人或受版权保护的作品的提示和上传。在 Suno 之外共享内容之前，该平台会添加嵌入的水印。

Visuals 可在网络、iOS 和 Android 上运行，并且需要自己的积分。 Pro 和 Premier 订阅者可以获得临时配额来试用。

7月下旬，慕尼黑地方法院在德国音乐权利组织GEMA提起的诉讼中做出了对Suno不利的裁决，认定Suno侵犯了版权。不久之后，Suno 宣布推出工具，将 Suno 制作的歌曲标记为其他平台上人工智能生成的歌曲。该公司已与华纳音乐达成协议，但环球和索尼仍在寻求诉讼。

news.summary_en: Osmo, founded by former Google Brain researcher Alex Wiltschko, has developed the first foundation model for smell using a proprietary dataset of 10 million human labels and 800 million 'scent tokens'. The model demonstrates human-level proficiency in identifying and synthesizing scents, outperforming professional perfumers in tests conducted by major global consumer goods companies.
news.article_content_en:
In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”

“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”

In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.)

The company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.

But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the company’s big claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows , has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack , arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. A representative for Osmo did not respond in time for publication.

Michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the company’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.

But even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very important for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”

In a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies .

For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.

“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. “So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”

news.article_content_zh:
在新泽西州纽瓦克机场附近的一个实验室里，一支由大约 30 名经验丰富的人类嗅探员组成的团队正在慢慢地寻找地球上的每一种气味。他们仔细的笔记——“坚果味”、“桃味”、“海洋味”——与化学分析交叉引用，为人工智能初创公司 Osmo 所说的世界上第一个嗅觉基础模型创建了一组丰富的训练数据。创始人 Alex Wiltschko 表示，该公司的目标是“让计算机拥有嗅觉”。

“气味分子确实是这个星球上大多数物种能说的唯一语言，”他说。 “大多数物种无法通过声音或视觉进行交流，所以它确实是地球的原始语言。从记忆和情感的角度来看，它对我们来说非常强大。你可以闻一次某种味道，并记住它的余生。你可以在街上闻到某种味道，然后被拉回高中。”

Wiltschko 声称，在过去的几个月里，Osmo 的模型已经实现了“人类水平的嗅觉智能”。该公司对此的定义是，该模型在检测和区分气味方面与普通人一样好，在创造气味方面与初级香水设计师一样好。该公司表示，其技术已被应用于香水行业，帮助品牌设计和制造新香水。该公司表示，上个月，Osmo 的人工智能模型优于全球最大消费品公司之一的内部调香师。威尔奇科认为，它最终可能会被部署用于机场威胁检测或诊断疾病等。

Wiltschko 于 2023 年从搜索巨头 Google Brain（这家搜索巨头的前人工智能研究实验室）的工作中剥离了这家初创公司，他正在运行与其他领域的人工智能初创公司相同的剧本：在困难问题上投入大量数据，看看会发生什么。威尔奇科说，气味的挑战在于缺乏良好的数据。据他统计，在 Osmo 出现之前，现有数据库中人类对气味的描述不足 20 万条。此外，收集数据所需的化学传感器设备价格昂贵，而且香水行业对其在嗅觉科学方面的工作保密。

该公司的大部分工作都是创建自己的数据集，其中包含超过 1000 万个人类标签和 8 亿个“气味标记”，这些标记描述了产生特定气味的确切分子和浓度。 Osmo 使用光谱仪和其他化学传感器全天候运行，分解从水果和鲜花到食品储藏室主食和器官的所有物质的分子组成。一支由大约 70 名美国和海外训练有素的数据贴标员组成的团队每天都在嗅闻东西，并使用标准化的香水词汇写下它们的气味。

以这种方式绘制气味图会排除一些不太可能的相似之处。就像改变单词的顺序可以极大地影响句子的含义一样，以不同比例重新排列气味分子可以极大地改变人类感知的气味。 “定义新生儿气味的气味标记与一盘新鲜煮熟的意大利面条中的气味标记有很大的重叠，”威尔奇科说。 （他说，特别是巴里拉（Barilla）品牌的意大利面，这可能会给面食工厂的人们带来一些问题。）

该公司还创造自己的香水，使用校车大小的气味打印机器人，根据精确的配方混合成分，为 Osmo 自己的研究制作样品，并为付费客户制作香水。它可以根据 ChatGPT 风格的提示设计和打印订购的气味。威尔奇科打开他的笔记本电脑，向我展示人工智能模型是如何工作的。他在屏幕上打开了一个文本框，我让他制作一款闻起来像葡萄牙蛋挞的香水（我们在里斯本参加网络峰会），针对 18 至 23 岁的男性。该系统花了几分钟思考，然后生成了三种与概要相匹配的潜在气味特征的选项（奶油味、椰子味、果味）以及创建它们所需的分子。如果我继续订购过程，我的招牌蛋奶之水大约一周后就会准备好。

Osmo 的技术已被用于制造零售香水，包括宝洁等巨头。盖茨基金会在 Osmo 推出时投资了 500 万美元，后来又向该公司提供了 350 万美元的赠款，用于评估驱除携带疾病的昆虫的分子，Osmo 确定了八种比避蚊胺更驱避的物质。 Osmo 还与在线服装市场 StockX 合作，通过检测鞋子所用材料的化学成分差异，利用气味来识别假冒运动鞋。

但并非所有人都相信这项技术或该公司的重大主张。气味科学家、《鼻子知道什么》一书的作者艾弗里·吉尔伯特 (Avery Gilbert) 在他的 Substack 上对 Osmo 提出了尖锐的批评，认为它的一些营销主张没有记录在案，而且它的专利申请仍然依赖于人类感官小组和调香师，而不是人工智能。 “对于一家以超酷人工智能为基础的公司来说，这种对人类感官判断的严重依赖似乎很奇怪，”他在三月份写道。 Osmo 的代表没有及时做出回应。

赫特福德郡大学前神经计算教授 Michael Schmuker 曾为 Osmo 提供咨询，他表示该公司的技术是一项成就。他与同事一起创建了 Osmo 2023 模型的开源逆向工程版本，但缺乏该公司此后收集的大量数据。

但即使有了所有这些气味数据，Osmo也可能遗漏了一些使人类嗅觉独特的因素，Schmuker说。“嗅觉是超级复杂的。环境对嗅觉非常重要。同样的分子可能会根据环境引起不同的联想，”他说。“像卡芒贝尔奶酪这样的法国奶酪的气味与用过的尿布中的分子部分相同。你不会因为上下文而混淆这两者。”

在像香水实验室这样的受控环境中，缺乏背景可能并不那么重要。但如果 Osmo 的技术如 Wiltschko 所说，成为人工智能世界模型的“嗅觉通道”，那么它可能会产生影响。想象一下，一台机器可以嗅出生产线上食物的腐败情况，或者通过气味检测肿瘤，就像狗在试点研究中接受的训练那样。

施穆克说，要实现这一目标，传感器技术需要变得更好。这些模型需要不断改进。医学诊断是最大的奖项。

“历史上有很多公司直接登上了这座山峰，但不幸的是，它们都没有成功，因为它非常昂贵，而且非常困难，”威尔奇科说。 “所以我们正在做的就是在所有这些山脉的山脚下建立这个基础。我们派遣探险队到山上进行探索，基本上是嗅遍整个世界。”

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 原Google Brain研究员Alex Wiltschko创立的初创公司Osmo，通过构建包含1000万人工标注与8亿“气味Token”的数据集，训练出首个气味基础模型。该模型在气味辨识与香水设计任务中，已表现出媲美人类嗅觉专家及初级香水设计师的性能，并在全球大型消费品公司的实测中超越了资深香水师。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Osmo, founded by former Google Brain researcher Alex Wiltschko, has developed the first foundation model for smell using a proprietary dataset of 10 million human labels and 800 million 'scent tokens'. news.summary_en: Lovable CEO Anton Osika and CTO Fabian Hedin announced a strategic pivot for their $13B-valued startup, evolving their 'vibe coding' platform into an automated business management engine. With 80% of users seeking financial gain but only 35% currently monetizing, the company aims to bridge this gap by integrating automated business strategy, web development, and customer retention tools.
news.article_content_en:
I squint my eyes in confusion when Anton Osika asks if I like cakes. The CEO of Lovable was in the middle of explaining how his AI startup, flush with investment cash and recently valued at over $13 billion, is ready to shift its focus after two years. Why does the vibe-coding king care if I like sweet treats? He thinks that if I do, I might be able to vibe code a living out of that.

The generative AI revolution completely flipped coding. Rather than a niche skill set where humans had to learn how to talk like computers, software development could be done by computers generating code in response to natural-language requests from humans.

Osika was early to this shift, launching a viral open-source tool in 2023, a precursor to Lovable. His mission? “Reduce barriers to build.” That initial spark ignited what is now one of Europe’s most dynamic startups.

Tech insiders talked nonstop last year about the transformative power of “vibe coding” that could empower anyone to build their own software. Parents could whip up custom apps to help track demanding club sports schedules. Picky eaters could create dynamic meal plans that adapt to whatever’s in their fridge. Polyamorous people could build software to manage their relationship hierarchies. Whatever random, niche software you can imagine, you can build it.

But Osika isn’t satisfied with helping millions of people vibe code apps for their everyday life—he also wants Lovable users to make more cash. The startup claims that around 80 percent of users arrive at the platform with a financial incentive, like building customer-facing platforms for online sales. That said, Lovable also reports that only 35 percent currently earn revenue with their projects.

That brings us back to the cake question. Lovable’s plan for next year is to help you run a small business based on your passions, like opening a cake shop. Fabian Hedin, Lovable’s other cofounder and chief technology officer, says the startup is building automations to help with everything from initial business strategy and website creation to long-term customer retention and marketing plans.

For example, a cake shop owner receives an AI-generated morning briefing through a chatbot-style, Lovable dashboard. “You set some goals, and then the AI is proactive in helping you reach those goals,” Hedin says. This briefing analyzes the number of cake boxes sold through a holiday promotion, customer emails it automatically answered, and reminders to make financial deposits on time.

Lovable has been a boon for savvy social media content creators, who can leverage their platforms better through vibe-coded sites. “People who have audiences themselves are building larger businesses around that,” Osika says. He recently went to a dinner in New York with creators, one of whom uses Lovable to help sell their book. Others have used it to help hawk merch.

Lovable earning the trust of burgeoning entrepreneurs is critical to the success of this new endeavor, though it may be an uphill battle. Vibe-coded projects were notorious for not necessarily being secure and sometimes exposing user data.

The startup was one of many vibe-coded services that came under fire this year for facilitating user-generated apps that exposed data on the open web. Earlier this month, Lovable revamped its security approach as part of its effort to make sites generated through its platform more secure by default.

“The moment real people use what you build, security is the product,” Igor Andriushchenko, Lovable’s head of security, tells WIRED. “That's why it's one of the areas we continue investing in the most and why we’ve built it directly into the platform experience.”

Osika will see Lovable as successful next year if he can help a new wave of entrepreneurs start sustainable businesses. Why just vibe code an app when you can vibe code a living?

news.article_content_zh:
当安东·奥西卡问我是否喜欢蛋糕时，我困惑地眯起眼睛。 Lovable 的首席执行官正在解释他的人工智能初创公司如何准备在两年后转移重心，该公司拥有充足的投资现金，最近估值超过 130 亿美元。为什么振动编码之王关心我是否喜欢甜食？他认为如果我这样做了，我也许可以靠编程为生。

生成式人工智能革命彻底颠覆了编码。软件开发不是人类必须学习如何像计算机一样说话的小众技能，而是可以通过计算机响应人类的自然语言请求生成代码来完成。

Osika 很早就实现了这一转变，于 2023 年推出了一款病毒式开源工具，这是 Lovable 的前身。他的使命？ “减少建设障碍。”最初的火花点燃了现在欧洲最具活力的初创公司之一。

去年，技术内部人士不停地谈论“vibe 编码”的变革力量，它可以让任何人都能够构建自己的软件。家长可以开发定制应用程序来帮助跟踪要求严格的俱乐部运动日程。挑食的人可以根据冰箱里的食物制定动态的膳食计划。多角恋的人可以构建软件来管理他们的关系层次结构。无论您能想象到什么随机的、小众的软件，您都可以构建它。

但 Osika 并不满足于帮助数百万人为日常生活编写应用程序，他还希望 Lovable 用户赚更多钱。该初创公司声称，大约 80% 的用户是带着经济激励来到该平台的，比如构建面向客户的在线销售平台。尽管如此，Lovable 还报告称，目前只有 35% 的人通过他们的项目获得收入。

这让我们回到了蛋糕问题。 Lovable 明年的计划是帮助你根据自己的兴趣经营一家小企业，比如开一家蛋糕店。 Lovable 的另一位联合创始人兼首席技术官 Fabian Hedin 表示，这家初创公司正在构建自动化技术，以帮助完成从最初的业务战略和网站创建到长期客户保留和营销计划的各个方面。

例如，蛋糕店老板通过聊天机器人风格的 Lovable 仪表板收到人工智能生成的早间简报。 “你设定一些目标，然后人工智能会主动帮助你实现这些目标，”赫丁说。本简报分析了通过假日促销销售的蛋糕盒数量、自动回复的客户电子邮件以及按时存入资金的提醒。

Lovable 对于精明的社交媒体内容创作者来说是一个福音，他们可以通过氛围编码网站更好地利用他们的平台。 “那些自己拥有受众的人正在围绕这一点建立更大的业务，”奥西卡说。他最近在纽约与创作者共进晚餐，其中一位创作者使用 Lovable 来帮助销售他们的书。其他人则用它来帮助推销商品。

赢得新兴企业家的信任对于这项新事业的成功至关重要，尽管这可能是一场艰苦的战斗。 Vibe 编码的项目因不一定安全且有时会暴露用户数据而臭名昭著。

该初创公司是今年因促进用户生成的应用程序在开放网络上公开数据而受到批评的众多振动编码服务之一。本月早些时候，Lovable 改进了其安全方法，努力使通过其平台生成的网站在默认情况下更加安全。

Lovable 的安全主管 Igor Andriushchenko 告诉《连线》杂志：“当真正的人们使用你构建的产品时，安全就是产品。” “这就是为什么它是我们继续投资最多的领域之一，也是我们将其直接构建到平台体验中的原因。”

如果 Osika 能够帮助新一波的企业家开创可持续发展的企业，Lovable 明年将会取得成功。当你可以通过 Vivi 编码谋生时，为什么只用 Vive 编码一个应用程序呢？

Thank you for being here today. As we speak, one of the most significant sets of cybersecurity events in history is happening, a set of critical security vulnerability disclosures that some are calling “Black October.” These vulnerabilities, which were found in some of the core infrastructure of the internet, were found by frontier AI systems, and their disclosure is part of an urgent effort to bolster software security worldwide. This is the urgent matter this month; next month there will be another. Software vulnerability discovery is the dual-use capability AI systems have arrived at today, but soon enough there will be another, and it will inspire its own urgent project to use the good side of the capability before malicious actors use the bad side. All of these urgent matters will overlap, inevitably, and much of what we today call “AI policy” is likely to be made amid this clamor.

But it is not the reactive and urgent things I’ve come to talk to you about today. Instead, I want to talk to you about where things might be headed in the bigger picture. It can be hard, amid such a barrage of urgency, to think about these more abstract and airy questions. But these questions matter, because without a sense of what long-term futures we’d like to achieve–and which we’d like to avoid–we might end up with a macro outcome we disfavor, even if we made wise decisions at every step along the way.

It is often remarked that the technology industry lacks a positive vision for where the things it is building will take us. I disagree: San Francisco and other hubs of entrepreneurship are filled with positive visions for our technological future. People really are building flying cars, autonomous vehicles, robots of many sizes and shapes, nuclear fusion, and, of course, artificial general intelligence. What we lack, instead, is a positive vision of our institutional future: how is this all going to work?

That is not to say, however, that there is no institutional vision for the future. Unfortunately, the vision I find most common is not one I would call positive. When it is articulated at all, it is usually in whispers. But more often, it is left unsaid, discernable only by implication. I call it the silent consensus.

Consider a company that can do almost everything without human labor. Its AI systems do research and development, make discoveries, negotiate contracts, allocate capital, and manufacture. Suppose it is better at these things than its human competitors, even when those humans augment their effort with AI. If human involvement serves only to slow the business down, human managers and owners will have a powerful incentive to take their hands off the wheel. If this occurs throughout the global economy, humans will be driven by the logic of market competition to forfeit their primacy over global commerce. Over time, the market may come to serve the demands of machines as much as, or more, than it serves the demands and wants of people.

What happens after that is anyone’s guess. Perhaps humans would benefit tremendously. If the machines who had subsumed us held humans in high intrinsic regard, we could become the beneficiaries of their labor and the wealth they generate. Or perhaps, being robbed of economic and increasingly political power, humans will find ourselves less and less relevant in the world, less and less able to shape the trajectory of world affairs. Maybe a small number of humans would hold extraordinary power and wealth, at the expense of a broadly disempowered mass, or maybe we all would share the same fate of disempowerment. Regardless of the specifics, the common thread that constitutes the silent consensus is the termination of human primacy in the world as we know it.

Nothing in these scenarios requires AI to rebel against its creators. Nothing requires its owners to wish for human disempowerment. Each decision to delegate can make sense on its own terms. Yet taken together, the decisions could produce a world in which people have forfeited effective authority over much of our civilization. Even if we make extraordinary progress on the bedeviling questions of AI safety and alignment, we could still find ourselves having submitted to a new kind of machine entity. In the happy version of the future, the silent consensus would tell us, that entity will be a kind one, a machine with the best interests of humans at heart. A machine, the Brautigan poem goes, of loving grace.

To these machines, the silent consensus tells us, we will hand over the keys to our companies, and more and more, our institutions of governance. They will run them more effectively, more efficiently, with better wisdom and better judgment than we humans can muster. And so we will, with time, take our hands off the steering wheel, and let the loving machines take over the driving. We will be like passengers in a car—a very nice car, perhaps a materially nicer car than we can dream of today—but passengers nonetheless, lacking control over where the vehicle is headed. To the extent that we work, it is mostly as a kind of ritual or play-acting, something more like a game to entertain our species.

Some observers will argue that the silent consensus rests on a false premise, because we humans do not control the world today to begin with. And this criticism is worth bearing in mind: there is no “we” who decides what to do. We live in a radically decentralized world, whether we like it or not. Yet this point should not make us complacent either: while “we” do not “control” the world, human beings collectively do have primacy over world affairs. There is no species of animal that seriously competes with us for control over resources. We should reject the intellectually sloppy notion that humans can exercise top-down control over the world, but we should not conflate that rejection with a denial of the obvious reality that humans are, collectively, the Earth’s prime actor.

Some people who are willing to articulate the silent consensus believe it is a genuinely good future. Others do not, but are resigned to its inevitability. The silent consensus is not a consensus because everyone agrees it is good, nor is it a secret plan among the people building AI. The consensus is simply that the forfeiture of human primacy over world affairs is inevitable, or at least that it is very difficult to imagine another vision for a future that is truly robust to superintelligent machines. A person can sincerely oppose that outcome while finding it difficult to conjure a plausible alternative vision. The fact that the consensus is mostly silent, sotto voce at best, is the tell.

I despise the silent consensus. I reject the forfeiture of human primacy. I detest the sense of inevitability. I remind myself that I could not look at my baby son in his beautiful eyes if I submitted to the silent consensus. And so to the silent consensus, I say no. And I believe the time has come to speak openly about the silent consensus, to shake ourselves out of our mostly unwitting acceptance of this vision.

The problem is this: the silent consensus became consensus for a reason. It is difficult to describe how humans will remain at the steering wheel alongside vastly superhuman machine intelligence. Most attempts to do so rely on arguments that AI is a mere tool, an instrument of pattern recognition not capable of “genuine understanding.” I fear these arguments are not robust to the reality of what is coming. I fear that they are their own form of complacency—a position based mostly in denial of what AI can do rather than a belief rooted in an affirmative vision for a human-led future. AIs cannot be said to lack “genuine understanding” even as they come to make progress on intellectual problems whose solutions have eluded humans for decades and centuries.

Why, then, do I believe humans must retain primacy? The easy answer is because I am a human being, and I am indeed an unapologetic human chauvinist.

But there is something deeper, too. Our primacy rests not in our intellect, not in maintaining our monopoly on “genuine understanding” indefinitely into the future. Our primacy rests instead on our past.

For it is we who came up out of the mud. We who forged primitive society out of dirt and stone. We who gazed up at the stars and asked why. We, with our fighting and our love and our envy and our joy, who discovered morality and ethics and law. It is we who sang and danced, wrote and composed. It is we who made history, and it is we who wrote it. That legacy is ours. The civilization we have built is a flame we have tended, and that flame belongs to us. Our past is a glorious inheritance over which we all are stewards, and part of that stewardship is our participation in what Michael Oakeshott called “the conversation of mankind,” that grand endeavor that began in primeval times.

Through that long and winding past, we forged a civilization that, in America, was conceived with the rights of the individual at the foundation, with reverence for the paths we all forge as we make our way through the world. Human beings have lives that can go better or worse: we bear the fruit of our wise decisions, and we bear the consequences when we err. The right to walk one’s own path does not turn on being the cleverest or the wisest. I do not lose my standing as a citizen because my neighbor has better judgment. I see no reason that the arrival of a more intelligent machine should dissolve that standing either, and indeed I see every reason to prevent that dissolution from occurring.

Some may argue that the machines, having read nearly the entire written record of this inheritance, are heirs too. And in some sense, they are. But a person who has read every letter in your family’s attic does not somehow become a member of your family. AI systems will come to join the conversation of mankind, first as observers and increasingly as participants, but they must not dominate it, nor render that conversation moot. To cede primacy is to betray our ancestors just as much as it is to betray our progeny. If this is not a fight worth having, no fight is worth having.

Now, I happen to believe that the adherents of the silent consensus are wrong about what machine superintelligence will be. That they are missing something important about how the world works, that they conflate intelligence with power. If you described the capabilities of even today’s AI systems to an adherent of the silent consensus five or ten years ago, they would probably have predicted that joblessness would be much higher now than it in fact is, and that human disempowerment writ large would be far further along than it actually is. I believe that human collective intelligence and capability is far greater than the adherents of the silent consensus suppose, and that our societies will prove more robust than they predict.

But I could be wrong. It may simply be the case, for example, that fully autonomous corporations outcompete human enterprise altogether. And if that is true, then the raw logic of economics will dictate that more and more capital be handed over to the machines. Disempowerment, in this future, does not require a machine overthrow of human civilization; it simply requires that the logic of capitalistic enterprise continue apace. Here, the AI revolution would find its closest analog in the agricultural revolution, when new modes of production fundamentally changed the architecture of human society. That this transformation was pleasant for the humans who experienced it is far from clear; indeed, there is substantial evidence that this transformation worsened human wellbeing for millennia.

I do not know if this is the future we face, and indeed I have argued elsewhere that I do not believe it is. But many of my colleagues—smart and caring and conscientious people—believe this is likely to be our future. If they are right, our fight against the silent consensus will be all the more challenging. We will have to swim against the current of economics, and in so doing, reject many of the things that are dogma for classical liberal individualists like me. This will be a perilous endeavor, one in which failure is far from improbable. But if this is not a fight worth having, no fight is worth having.

Retaining primacy means retaining accountability for humans and human institutions. That means AI developers should be accountable when they engage in unsafe development practices, but it also means that people and firms using AI should be held accountable when it is their misuse or lack of oversight that causes harm. This requires not just the law, but the technical infrastructure of accountability. People must be tied to the actions of their agents, and agents untethered to a human–if they are to be permitted at all to engage in the legitimate economy–must do so under guardrails. Any ability for agents to autonomously form corporations, own property, or litigate should be granted with extraordinary caution, if at all.

And in my industry, we can start to think seriously about how to build intelligent machines that are compatible with human primacy. We can build agents whose permissions are intelligible and limited, whose actions can be audited, and whose authority users can withdraw. Accountability for actions that materially affect others need not entail surveillance of ordinary private life or the end of anonymous speech. We can make commitments to user privacy and individual sovereignty over their digital property and data, including the practical ability to take that data elsewhere. We can design systems that help people acquire understanding and make decisions, as well as systems that carry out tasks. And we can test whether the products we build leave their users more capable of acting in the world.

None of this is a complete blueprint for a society with superhuman intelligence. I would distrust anyone who claimed to possess one. But it is a place to begin.

The future is shrouded in a thick fog. But we can still act today. Collectively, we can, for one thing, name the silent consensus aloud, expose its contours to the light of day. We can, each of us, radically widen the scope of our ambition. We can choose not to let AI shrink us, and instead do the hard work of letting it enlarge us. We can learn to ask ever-bolder questions, to interrogate the world with new verve and ferocity, and to wield our powerful machines in so doing. We can become a new kind of man—not a transhuman, but a man expanded.

I think about this when I look at my baby son. I do not wish for him merely to be watched over by benevolent machines, however comfortable a life they might provide. I want him to inherit a world in which he can ask questions no one has thought to ask, build things no one has thought to build. I do not want him to have a nicer car with a plusher passenger seat. I want him to have the wheel.
