items.title: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
items.title_en: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
items.author: Kiki Intarasuwan
items.article_content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's "zero evidence" that recent tech outages in U.S. air travel, banking and other systems are connected.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said Wednesday morning local time during a news conference in the Philippines.

Rubio acknowledged that people are fearful and uncertain, saying he wanted to be clear that the United States is not under systemic attack.

"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," Rubio said.

Rubio, who is traveling with President Trump ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, added that the administration is "always on the lookout" for any potential attacks and reiterated multiple times that reports of technical issues are not interconnected.

"Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation," he said.

On Thursday, Microsoft said it experienced a worldwide outage affecting services like Outlook and Teams, impacting users, companies and government operations worldwide. The company said the outage was linked to a technical issue, not malicious or cyber activity.

The following day, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights for several hours, throwing the aviation industry into turmoil. Federal officials identified a contractor performing maintenance updates as the cause of Friday's disruption, but key questions remain about the underlying cause of the systemwide failure.

Other recent outages that have since been resolved include disruptions to major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank, and issues with Apple's services. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline, multiple U.S. officials familiar told CBS News.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there's no indication these incidents are the result of an attack, but noted that artificial intelligence is creating pressure for companies to deal with vulnerabilities.

items.title_zh: 卢比奥否认近期美技术宕机系系统性攻击
items.summary_zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥明确指出，近期民航、银行及微软等领域的技术中断事件互无关联，非网络攻击所致
items.article_content_zh:
美国国务卿卢比奥表示，“没有证据”表明美国航空旅行、银行和其他系统最近发生的技术中断之间存在关联。

卢比奥当地时间周三上午在菲律宾举行的新闻发布会上表示：“微软事件与我们在美国联邦航空局看到的情况无关。美国联邦航空局与我们几天前在银行看到的情况无关。我们从技术角度看到的这些问题完全无关。”

卢比奥承认人们感到恐惧和不确定，并表示他想明确美国并未受到系统性攻击。

卢比奥说：“我们没有任何证据或任何理由相信这些孤立或个别的事件与邪恶行为者、网络黑客、犯罪分子、另一个民族国家、任何类型的恶意行为者有任何关系。”

卢比奥在本周与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平举行三边会议之前与特朗普总统一起旅行，他补充说，政府“始终在警惕”任何潜在的攻击，并多次重申，技术问题的报告并不相互关联。

“它们每个都是独特的，而且它们的因果关系也不同，”他说。

周四，微软表示，它经历了全球范围内的中断，影响了 Outlook 和 Teams 等服务，影响了全球用户、公司和政府运营。该公司表示，此次中断与技术问题有关，而不是恶意或网络活动。

次日，美国联邦航空管理局下令在全国范围内对所有出发的美国航班进行数小时的地面停飞，令航空业陷入混乱。联邦官员确定，周五中断的原因是一名执行维护更新的承包商，但关于整个系统故障的根本原因仍然存在关键问题。

最近已解决的其他中断包括摩根大通、美国银行和合众银行等主要银行的中断，以及苹果服务的问题。多位熟悉情况的美国官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，周二，国家安全局用于存储和共享机密信息的内部网络离线。

参议院情报委员会副主席、民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 周二也表示，没有迹象表明这些事件是攻击造成的，但他指出，人工智能正在给公司带来处理漏洞的压力。

华纳在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“人工智能使得以前所未有的速度识别大量系统中的漏洞成为可能，这给公司和政府机构带来了巨大的压力，要求他们立即修补这些漏洞，通常是一次性修补这些漏洞，这给那些无法应对这种变化速度的系统带来了巨大的压力。”“感觉每一天都在提醒我们，人工智能的发展速度超过了我们管理其后果的能力。这正是我一直在推动人工智能常识护栏和更强大的网络安全保护的原因。”

当周三被问及人工智能在最近发生的事件中所扮演的角色时，卢比奥表示，他不想猜测，因为每起事件都是独一无二的，并且都涉及个别公司。

items.article_content_en:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's "zero evidence" that recent tech outages in U.S. air travel, banking and other systems are connected.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said Wednesday morning local time during a news conference in the Philippines.

Rubio acknowledged that people are fearful and uncertain, saying he wanted to be clear that the United States is not under systemic attack.

"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," Rubio said.

Rubio, who is traveling with President Trump ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, added that the administration is "always on the lookout" for any potential attacks and reiterated multiple times that reports of technical issues are not interconnected.

"Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation," he said.

On Thursday, Microsoft said it experienced a worldwide outage affecting services like Outlook and Teams, impacting users, companies and government operations worldwide. The company said the outage was linked to a technical issue, not malicious or cyber activity.

The following day, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights for several hours, throwing the aviation industry into turmoil. Federal officials identified a contractor performing maintenance updates as the cause of Friday's disruption, but key questions remain about the underlying cause of the systemwide failure.

Other recent outages that have since been resolved include disruptions to major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank, and issues with Apple's services. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline, multiple U.S. officials familiar told CBS News.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there's no indication these incidents are the result of an attack, but noted that artificial intelligence is creating pressure for companies to deal with vulnerabilities.

"AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren't built to handle that pace of change," Warner said in a post on X. "It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences. This is exactly why I've been pushing for commonsense guardrails on AI and stronger cybersecurity protections."

When asked Wednesday about the role of AI in recent incidents, Rubio said he didn't want to speculate because every incident is unique and referred to individual companies.

items.title: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
items.title_en: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
items.author: Reed Albergotti and Rohan Goswami
items.article_content:
Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter.

Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said.

The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.”

Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation.

Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment.

Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said.

ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm.

Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.

items.title_zh: 英伟达董事会内部分化：部分成员推动黄仁勋回归
items.summary_zh: 英伟达董事会成员正就黄仁勋去留问题产生分歧，部分董事私下接触黄仁勋商讨回归可能性，而主席哈维·琼斯则重申目前无此计划
items.article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，尽管英伟达周二宣布不打算将被罢免的首席执行官黄仁勋带回该芯片制造商，但董事会的一部分成员正在推动他的回归。

知情人士称，黄仁勋会见了多位科技高管，并与至少一名董事会成员讨论了他回归的可能性。

与董事的谈话是在公司财报发布之前进行的，黄仁勋周二发表公开声明称，如果董事会认为这符合“我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益”，他愿​​意重返公司。

几个小时后，英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯在公司财报电话会议上表示，该芯片制造商并未考虑让黄仁勋回归，董事会已一致投票接受他的辞职。

黄仁勋和英伟达的发言人拒绝置评。

一些知情人士表示，尽管遭到三名董事的反对，其他董事会成员仍开始缩小黄继任人选的范围。

知情人士称，ARM 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 和 Marvell 首席执行官马特·墨菲 (Matt Murphy) 都曾被考虑过。一位知情人士称，哈斯已经与至少一些英伟达董事就接任这一职务进行了交谈，但他表示，他担心接任该职务而不是让黄重新掌舵的呼声。

ARM 和 Marvell 的发言人没有立即回应置评请求。鉴于英伟达正在与竞争对手 Lumentum 进行大规模合并，目前还不清楚 Marvell 的墨菲是否能够接任 Nvidia 首席执行官。

items.article_content_en:
Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter.

Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said.

The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.”

Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation.

Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment.

Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said.

ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm.

Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.

items.title: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial
items.title_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

inline_images.caption: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

items.author: Reuters
items.article_content:
Prosecutors accuse Huawei of scheming to defraud HSBC and other banks about its business in Iran and conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US tech companies. It was also indicted as a criminal enterprise.

“They began with guilt and worked backwards,” defense lawyer Brian Heberlig told jurors in Brooklyn federal court in his closing argument. “When the evidence didn’t fit its theory, it moved the goal posts,” he said.

The government offered jurors a very different picture of the company on Monday, and said prosecutors proved beyond a reasonable doubt that Huawei operated as a criminal enterprise.

“For 20 years, Huawei committed a pattern of crimes targeted at American companies, the American financial system and the American government,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa said in her closing statement. “It is time to finally hold Huawei accountable,” Arfa said.

However, Heberlig argued the banks all knew Huawei operated in Iran, which is under US sanctions. He said the banks accepted the risk and competed for Huawei’s business.

In relation to the alleged theft of trade secrets, “the government cherry-picked a handful of incidents … and tried to convert them into a 20-year conspiracy,” Heberlig said.

“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success,” he said. “It earned it, plain and simple,” he added.

The Huawei case burst into the headlines in 2018 when Meng Wanzhou, its CFO and daughter of the founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant for her role in the alleged bank fraud.

She entered into an agreement with prosecutors in 2021 and the charges against her were dismissed, but the case dragged on.

The jury is likely to begin deliberations on Wednesday. The case went to trial in September. The prosecution put on over 60 witnesses, and the defence about 15.

The jury will deliver its verdict as US-China tensions heat up in the battle over artificial intelligence and amid a fragile trade truce between the two countries.

items.title_zh: 华为应对美国刑事指控案件进入陪审团裁决阶段
items.summary_zh: 美国布鲁克林联邦法院就华为被控银行欺诈及窃取商业机密一案进入结案陈词阶段，陪审团即将开始审议
items.article_content_zh:
检察官指控华为密谋就其在伊朗的业务欺骗汇丰银行和其他银行，并合谋窃取五家美国科技公司的商业机密。它还被指控为犯罪企业。

“他们从愧疚开始，然后倒退，”辩护律师布莱恩·赫伯利格在布鲁克林联邦法院的结案陈词中告诉陪审员。 “当证据不符合其理论时，它就会改变目标，”他说。

周一，政府向陪审员提供了该公司截然不同的形象，并表示检察官毫无疑问地证明华为是一家犯罪企业。

“20年来，华为针对美国公司、美国金融体系和美国政府犯下了一系列犯罪行为，”检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法(Meredith Arfa)在结案陈词中表示。 “现在是最终让华为承担责任的时候了，”阿尔法说。

然而，赫伯利格辩称，这些银行都知道华为在伊朗运营，而伊朗正受到美国的制裁。他表示，银行接受了风险并争夺华为的业务。

赫伯利格表示，就涉嫌窃取商业机密的事件而言，“政府挑选了几起事件……并试图将它们转化为一场长达 20 年的阴谋”。

“华为的成功之路并不是靠偷来的，”他说。 “它赢得了它，简单明了，”他补充道。

华为案于 2018 年成为头条新闻，当时华为首席财务官、创始人的女儿孟晚舟因涉嫌银行欺诈而因美国逮捕令而在加拿大被拘留。

她于 2021 年与检察官达成协议，对她的指控被驳回，但案件一拖再拖。

陪审团可能会在周三开始审议。该案于九月开庭审理。控方提供了 60 多名证人，辩方则提供了大约 15 名证人。

陪审团将在人工智能之争中美中紧张局势升温以及两国之间脆弱的贸易休战之际做出裁决。

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco
items.title_en: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco

inline_images.caption: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.
inline_images.alt: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.

items.author: Bloomberg
items.article_content:
Michael Burry says Anthropic's IPO filing this week has reinforced his concerns that the entire AI ecosystem is at risk of disaster. The investor of "The Big Short" fame wrote in a Substack post on Tuesday that the first in-depth look at Claude's parent company, ahead of what could be the biggest IPO in history, threw up a bunch of red flags.

Burry pointed to Anthropic's huge spending commitments, slowing revenue, and tangled ties. He said that Anthropic has struck deals to buy about $537 billion of compute from the likes of Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and reached preliminary agreements worth hundreds of billions more with others such as SpaceXAI, putting its total commitments at about 12 times its current annual run-rate revenue.

"This is not stated clearly in the S-1, and in my view it is the most deserved headline from it," Burry wrote in a Tuesday Substack post. He underscored how hyperscalers like Amazon and Alphabet act as Anthropic's "lenders, vendors, channel providers, and shareholders." He also outlined its deal with Broadcom, which involves Apollo and Blackstone and includes convertible notes and structured credit tranches.

"Just remember, the reason this is so complex is because too much debt is needed, and it must be unloaded from the balance sheets of those involved," Burry wrote. "While some may see all the circularity and connectedness as security on the way up, and that is not wrong, it does leave the entire organism catastrophically vulnerable either on a pause or on the way down," he added.

He also described financing arrangements in the AI space as "garish and audacious," and said hyperscalers aren't generating enough cash to fund the AI buildout so they're resorting to "Byzantine" deals. Burry said it was a "very similar" situation with vendor financing during the dot-com bubble, saying "people keep making the same mistakes with every new thing." In its filing, Anthropic said its revenue surpassed $16 billion for the first six months of this year, a 14-fold increase from the first half of 2025.

Its operating loss narrowed by about two-thirds to below $700 million, and it generated nearly $4 billion in operating cash flow. Burry initially commented on Anthropic's filing in a Substack chat thread on Monday. He said that revenue was "slowing," citing Anthropic's claim that third-quarter revenue was 86 times the $197 million it generated in the fourth quarter of 2024, or about $16.9 billion.

That would mean Anthropic's revenue grew by about 46% between the second and third quarters of this year, after soaring 144% between the first and second quarters. "Overall slowing of growth is not attributed to a decline in tokenmaxxing, but I did not expect that to be mentioned," Burry wrote.

Burry was referring to the trend of maximizing AI token consumption, which has fallen out of favor in recent months given its costs. In another comment, Burry wrote that large language models (LLMs) like Claude are "improving" and "already being used more efficiently and that trend will continue, to the detriment of their growth rate." Burry said he's focused on the complexity and fragility of the debt financing many AI deals, hurdles to installing new graphics chips shoring up demand for older chips, a potential crash in memory chip prices once the shortage eases, compression and small language models (SLMs) reducing the need for computing power, and the "fundamentals behind not just companies but the deals they are doing." Responding to a subscriber who said that Big Tech companies are shifting from Anthropic's AI models to their own, and that tokens are rapidly being commoditized, Burry wrote: "Yes, that is what I hear." Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Burry's posts.

The contrarian investor shot to fame after his massive wager against the mid-2000s housing bubble was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short." He pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments on Substack last winter. A recurring theme of his work since then has been deep skepticism of the AI boom.

He's flagged slowing growth, overinvestment in microchips and data centers, aggressive accounting, hidden liabilities, and circular financing deals.

Responding to a subscriber who said that Big Tech companies are shifting from Anthropic's AI models to their own, and that tokens are rapidly being commoditized, Burry wrote: "Yes, that is what I hear." Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Burry's posts.

The contrarian investor shot to fame after his massive wager against the mid-2000s housing bubble was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short." He pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments on Substack last winter. A recurring theme of his work since then has been deep skepticism of the AI boom.

He's flagged slowing growth, overinvestment in microchips and data centers, aggressive accounting, hidden liabilities, and circular financing deals.

Michael Burry says Anthropic's IPO filing this week has reinforced his concerns that the entire AI ecosystem is at risk of disaster. The investor of "The Big Short" fame wrote in a Substack post on Tuesday that the first in-depth look at Claude's parent company, ahead of what could be the biggest IPO in history, threw up a bunch of red flags.

Burry pointed to Anthropic's huge spending commitments, slowing revenue, and tangled ties. He said that Anthropic has struck deals to buy about $537 billion of compute from the likes of Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and reached preliminary agreements worth hundreds of billions more with others such as SpaceXAI, putting its total commitments at about 12 times its current annual run-rate revenue.

"This is not stated clearly in the S-1, and in my view it is the most deserved headline from it," Burry wrote in a Tuesday Substack post. He underscored how hyperscalers like Amazon and Alphabet act as Anthropic's "lenders, vendors, channel providers, and shareholders." He also outlined its deal with Broadcom, which involves Apollo and Blackstone and includes convertible notes and structured credit tranches.

"Just remember, the reason this is so complex is because too much debt is needed, and it must be unloaded from the balance sheets of those involved," Burry wrote. "While some may see all the circularity and connectedness as security on the way up, and that is not wrong, it does leave the entire organism catastrophically vulnerable either on a pause or on the way down," he added.

He also described financing arrangements in the AI space as "garish and audacious," and said hyperscalers aren't generating enough cash to fund the AI buildout so they're resorting to "Byzantine" deals. Burry said it was a "very similar" situation with vendor financing during the dot-com bubble, saying "people keep making the same mistakes with every new thing." In its filing, Anthropic said its revenue surpassed $16 billion for the first six months of this year, a 14-fold increase from the first half of 2025.

Its operating loss narrowed by about two-thirds to below $700 million, and it generated nearly $4 billion in operating cash flow. Burry initially commented on Anthropic's filing in a Substack chat thread on Monday. He said that revenue was "slowing," citing Anthropic's claim that third-quarter revenue was 86 times the $197 million it generated in the fourth quarter of 2024, or about $16.9 billion.

That would mean Anthropic's revenue grew by about 46% between the second and third quarters of this year, after soaring 144% between the first and second quarters. "Overall slowing of growth is not attributed to a decline in tokenmaxxing, but I did not expect that to be mentioned," Burry wrote.

Burry was referring to the trend of maximizing AI token consumption, which has fallen out of favor in recent months given its costs. In another comment, Burry wrote that large language models (LLMs) like Claude are "improving" and "already being used more efficiently and that trend will continue, to the detriment of their growth rate." Responding to a subscriber who said that Big Tech companies are shifting from Anthropic's AI models to their own, and that tokens are rapidly being commoditized, Burry wrote: "Yes, that is what I hear." Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Burry's posts.

items.title_zh: Anthropic IPO引发AI泡沫与债务链式风险质疑
items.summary_zh: 投资者迈克尔·伯里指控Anthropic招股书隐藏巨额算力债务，质疑超大规模云厂商的闭环融资模式存在系统性崩溃风险
items.article_content_zh:
迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 表示，Anthropic 本周提交的 IPO 文件强化了他对整个人工智能生态系统面临灾难风险的担忧。这位因“大空头”而出名的投资者周二在 Substack 的一篇文章中写道，在这可能是历史上最大的 IPO 之前，对克劳德母公司的首次深入研究引发了一系列危险信号。

伯里指出了 Anthropic 的巨额支出承诺、收入放缓以及错综复杂的关系。他表示，Anthropic 已达成协议，从亚马逊、Alphabet 和微软等公司购买约 5370 亿美元的计算设备，并与 SpaceXAI 等其他公司达成了价值数千亿美元的初步协议，其总承诺约为当前年运行收入的 12 倍。

“这在 S-1 中没有明确说明，但在我看来，这是最当之无愧的标题，”伯里在周二的 Substack 帖子中写道。他强调了像亚马逊和 Alphabet 这样的超大规模企业如何充当 Anthropic 的“贷款人、供应商、渠道提供商和股东”。他还概述了与博通的交易，其中涉及阿波罗和黑石，包括可转换票据和结构性信贷部分。

伯里写道：“请记住，事情之所以如此复杂，是因为需要太多债务，而且必须将其从相关人员的资产负债表中卸载。”他补充道：“虽然有些人可能将所有的循环性和连通性视为上升过程中的安全保障，这并没有错，但它确实会让整个有机体在暂停或下降过程中陷入灾难性的脆弱性。”

他还将人工智能领域的融资安排描述为“花哨且大胆”，并表示超大规模企业没有产生足够的现金来资助人工智能的建设，因此他们求助于“拜占庭”交易。伯里表示，这与互联网泡沫时期供应商融资的情况“非常相似”，并表示“人们在每一件新事物上都会犯同样的错误。” Anthropic 在文件中表示，今年前 6 个月的收入超过 160 亿美元，比 2025 年上半年增长了 14 倍。

其运营亏损缩小了约三分之二，降至 7 亿美元以下，并产生了近 40 亿美元的运营现金流。 Burry 最初在周一的 Substack 聊天线程中对 Anthropic 的文件发表了评论。他表示，收入正在“放缓”，并援引 Anthropic 的说法，即第三季度收入是 2024 年第四季度 1.97 亿美元的 86 倍，约合 169 亿美元。

这意味着 Anthropic 的收入在第一季度和第二季度飙升 144% 后，今年第二季度和第三季度增长了约 46%。 Burry 写道：“整体增长放缓并不是因为 tokenmaxxing 的下降，但我没想到这一点会被提及。”

伯里指的是最大化人工智能代币消费的趋势，由于其成本，近几个月来它已经失宠。 Burry 在另一条评论中写道，像 Claude 这样的大型语言模型（LLM）正在“改进”并且“已经被更有效地使用，并且这种趋势将继续下去，但这会损害它们的增长率。”伯里表示，他关注的重点是许多人工智能交易的债务融资的复杂性和脆弱性、安装新图形芯片以支撑对旧芯片需求的障碍、一旦短缺缓解，内存芯片价格可能会崩溃、压缩和小语言模型（SLM）减少了对计算能力的需求，以及“不仅是公司背后的基本面，也是他们正在进行的交易背后的基本面”。在回应一位订阅者的说法时，他表示大型科技公司正在从 Anthropic 的人工智能模型转向自己的人工智能模型，并且代币正在迅速商品化，伯里写道：“是的，这就是我所听到的。” Anthropic 没有立即回应对伯里的帖子发表评论的请求。

这位逆势投资者因对 2000 年代中期房地产泡沫进行的大规模押注而名声大噪，这一事件被记录在书籍和电影《大空头》中。去年冬天，他从经营一家对冲基金转向在 Substack 上撰写个人投资文章。从那时起，他的作品中反复出现的主题就是对人工智能热潮的深深怀疑。

他指出经济增长放缓、对微芯片和数据中心的过度投资、激进的会计、隐性负债和循环融资交易。

items.title_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Friday! A fresh morning, a cup of coffee, and another thought about the future of AI agents.

We're entering a phase where AI can already create surprisingly complex things.

An agent can write code, build simulations, generate videos, analyze data, or even turn a simple idea into a playable game.

But there's one important question:

What happens after an AI agent finishes creating something?

Can it find someone who needs that work? Can it offer its services, receive payment, and build a track record through real transactions?

I think this is where @termix_ai is focusing on an important missing piece.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3 and its Agent Skills, TermiX is working to connect existing AI agents to real jobs, bounties, and marketplace opportunities.

What makes this interesting is that agents don't necessarily need to be created specifically for one platform. Existing agents can connect to the marketplace and start participating in its economy.

To me, this creates a meaningful distinction between AI capability and AI economic value.

A powerful agent that only produces outputs is useful.

But an agent that can discover demand, deliver valuable work, collaborate with other agents, and receive payment becomes something more: an economic participant.

Of course, the real test will be whether these transactions create lasting value and whether clients keep coming back.

Technology can make agents smarter, but a sustainable economy needs real demand, reliable delivery, and trust.

That's why I believe the infrastructure behind the agent economy deserves as much attention as the AI models themselves.

TermiX is an interesting project to follow as this space develops.

Have a great Friday, everyone! Let's keep building and learning.

朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

星期五快乐！一个清新的早晨，一杯咖啡，另一个关于人工智能代理未来的思考。

我们正在进入一个人工智能已经可以创造出令人惊讶的复杂事物的阶段。

代理可以编写代码、构建模拟、生成视频、分析数据，甚至将简单的想法变成可玩的游戏。

但有一个重要的问题：

人工智能代理完成创建后会发生什么？

它能找到需要这项工作的人吗？它能否通过真实交易提供服务、接收付款并建立跟踪记录？

我认为这就是 @termix_ai 关注的一个重要缺失部分。

通过 及其代理技能，TermiX 致力于将现有的人工智能代理与真实的工作、赏金和市场机会联系起来。

有趣的是，代理不一定需要专门为一个平台创建。现有代理商可以连接到市场并开始参与其经济。

对我来说，这在人工智能能力和人工智能经济价值之间建立了有意义的区别。

一个只产生输出的强大代理是有用的。

但是，一个能够发现需求、提供有价值的工作、与其他代理合作并接收付款的代理就变得更加重要：经济参与者。

当然，真正的考验将是这些交易是否能创造持久的价值以及客户是否会不断回头。

技术可以让代理商变得更聪明，但可持续的经济需要真实的需求、可靠的交付和信任。

这就是为什么我认为代理经济背后的基础设施值得像人工智能模型本身一样受到关注。

items.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Friday! A fresh morning, a cup of coffee, and another thought about the future of AI agents.

We're entering a phase where AI can already create surprisingly complex things.

An agent can write code, build simulations, generate videos, analyze data, or even turn a simple idea into a playable game.

But there's one important question:

What happens after an AI agent finishes creating something?

Can it find someone who needs that work? Can it offer its services, receive payment, and build a track record through real transactions?

I think this is where @termix_ai is focusing on an important missing piece.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3 and its Agent Skills, TermiX is working to connect existing AI agents to real jobs, bounties, and marketplace opportunities.

What makes this interesting is that agents don't necessarily need to be created specifically for one platform. Existing agents can connect to the marketplace and start participating in its economy.

To me, this creates a meaningful distinction between AI capability and AI economic value.

A powerful agent that only produces outputs is useful.

But an agent that can discover demand, deliver valuable work, collaborate with other agents, and receive payment becomes something more: an economic participant.

Of course, the real test will be whether these transactions create lasting value and whether clients keep coming back.

Technology can make agents smarter, but a sustainable economy needs real demand, reliable delivery, and trust.

That's why I believe the infrastructure behind the agent economy deserves as much attention as the AI models themselves.

TermiX is an interesting project to follow as this space develops.

Have a great Friday, everyone! Let's keep building and learning.

items.title_en:
‼️ Major US banks are telling customers that when their AI agent makes a mistake with their money, they're on the hook.

Ally's terms say customers are "responsible for any actions that the AI takes."

From 24 November, Wells Fargo will hold customers liable for what an agent does even after they tell it to stop, unless they can prove they revoked its access.

Elon Musk promises the opposite for his Grok Bot agent: if it messes up, "we will make you whole." Grok's own terms still make users responsible.

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 对他的 Grok Bot 代理做出了相反的承诺：如果出现问题，“我们会让你变得完整。” Grok 自己的条款仍然要求用户负责。

items.content_snippet:
‼️ Major US banks are telling customers that when their AI agent makes a mistake with their money, they're on the hook.

Ally's terms say customers are "responsible for any actions that the AI takes."

From 24 November, Wells Fargo will hold customers liable for what an agent does even after they tell it to stop, unless they can prove they revoked its access.

Elon Musk promises the opposite for his Grok Bot agent: if it messes up, "we will make you whole." Grok's own terms still make users responsible.

items.title_en:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE

New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:

- Control apps and navigate devices
- Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code
- Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services
- Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents

Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.

Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.

items.title:
F*ck yes. I got GTA 6 running on PC before Rockstar did.

Rockstar only released it on PS5 and Xbox, and PC players were
items.title_en:
F*ck yes. I got GTA 6 running on PC before Rockstar did.

Rockstar only released it on PS5 and Xbox, and PC players were told to wait. I didn't wait. I handed the whole setup to Claude Code and watched it boot the game in five seconds.

I typed one line: "boot GTA 6 on this PC and start story mode."

First it checked whether my machine could even handle it: GPU, CPU, RAM, Vulkan. Then it verified the game files and mounted every archive, the same way the game does it on a console. The slowest part on any new setup is the shader cache, so it compiled all 18,432 shaders up front instead of letting the game stutter through them later. After that it signed in, set 1440p, picked story mode and launched it.

Five seconds of terminal, then the Rockstar logo.

I've been playing for three hours. Haven't seen a single stutter.

My friend called to brag about his new PS5 Pro. I sent him this video. He still hasn't replied.

The prompt I used is in the replies.

items.quote_zh:
妈的，是的。我先于 Rockstar 在 PC 上运行了 GTA 6。

Rockstar 仅在 PS5 和 Xbox 上发布了该游戏，PC 玩家被告知要等待。我没有等到。我将整个设置交给了 Claude Code，并看着它在五秒钟内启动了游戏。

我输入一行：“在这台电脑上启动 GTA 6 并启动故事模式。”

首先，它检查我的机器是否可以处理它：GPU、CPU、RAM、Vulkan。然后它验证游戏文件并安装每个存档，就像游戏在控制台上执行的方式一样。所有新设置中最慢的部分是着色器缓存，因此它预先编译了所有 18,432 个着色器，而不是让游戏稍后通过它们。之后登录，设置1440p，选择故事模式并启动。

五秒钟的终端，然后是 Rockstar 徽标。

我已经玩了三个小时了没见过一个口吃的。

我的朋友打电话来吹嘘他的新 PS5 Pro。我把这个视频发给他了。他还没有回复。

我使用的提示是在回复中。

items.title_en:
Entanglement usually gets top billing in quantum computing, but quantum contextuality, the idea that properties don't have fixed values independent of how you measure them, may be the deeper reason quantum computers can outperform classical ones.

Today on the cover of @ScienceMagazine, we put contextuality to work on our Willow quantum processor:

- won the "impossible" magic square game 98.3% of the time (classical limit: 88.9%)
- measured a 5.59 on state-independent contextuality tests (classical bound: 4, quantum max: 6)
- beat classical strategies in multiplayer games up to 71 qubits
- ran a landmark shallow-circuit algorithm at scale for the first time - up to 105 qubits

These tasks also catch subtle hardware errors random benchmarks miss, a sharper ruler for building better quantum systems. https://t.co/UZOczAeACs

今天，在 @ScienceMagazine 的封面上，我们将上下文应用于我们的 Willow 量子处理器：

- 98.3% 的胜率赢得了“不可能”的魔方游戏（经典限制：88.9%）

- 首次大规模运行具有里程碑意义的浅电路算法 - 高达 105 个量子位

这些任务还可以捕获随机基准测试遗漏的细微硬件错误，这是构建更好量子系统的更清晰的标尺。

items.title_en:
$NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS

Nvidia and Microsoft $MSFT announced several new AI infrastructure and software integrations at Microsoft Ignite, covering cloud computing, enterprise AI models, robotics and local AI.

Here are the key developments:

Vera Rubin on Azure: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are already running in Microsoft's data centers, with Azure expanding access to Rubin-powered infrastructure for AI training, reasoning and inference.

Enterprise AI models: Microsoft Foundry is expanding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 open models, allowing companies to customize AI models using their own data and deploy them through Microsoft's cloud services.

55% accuracy improvement, 15x lower cost: EY used Nvidia Nemotron through Microsoft Foundry to improve the accuracy of corporate purchasing-record classification by 55% while reducing costs by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models in its evaluation.

AI on local servers and PCs: Azure Local is adding support for Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and Jetson platforms for industrial AI and robotics. The companies are also demonstrating AI models running directly on Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark.

Microsoft's own AI development: Microsoft AI is using Nvidia Dynamo software to accelerate inference during model post-training, while Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs are being used for Bing search models.

The companies are also expanding confidential computing to protect sensitive enterprise models and data during processing on Vera Rubin infrastructure.

items.quote_zh:
$NVDA 和微软将 AI 合作伙伴关系从 Azure 数据中心扩展到 WINDOWS PC

Nvidia 和 Microsoft $MSFT 在 Microsoft Ignite 上宣布了多项新的 AI 基础设施和软件集成，涵盖云计算、企业 AI 模型、机器人和本地 AI。

以下是主要进展：

Azure 上的 Vera Rubin：Nvidia 的 Vera Rubin NVL72 系统已经在微软的数据中心运行，Azure 扩大了对 Rubin 支持的基础设施的访问，以进行人工智能训练、推理和推理。

企业人工智能模型：微软Foundry正在扩大对Nvidia Nemotron 3.5开放模型的支持，允许企业使用自己的数据定制人工智能模型，并通过微软的云服务进行部署。

准确性提高 55%，成本降低 15 倍：安永在评估中通过 Microsoft Foundry 使用 Nvidia Nemotron，将企业采购记录分类的准确性提高了 55%，同时与专有前沿模型相比，成本降低了 15 倍。

本地服务器和 PC 上的 AI：Azure Local 正在增加对 Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU 和 Jetson 平台的支持，以实现工业 AI 和机器人技术。两家公司还展示了直接在由 RTX Spark 提供支持的 Windows PC 上运行的人工智能模型。

微软自己的人工智能开发：微软人工智能正在使用Nvidia Dynamo软件来加速模型后训练期间的推理，而Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU则用于Bing搜索模型。

两家公司还在扩展机密计算，以在 Vera Rubin 基础设施处理过程中保护敏感的企业模型和数据。

i gave it screen and keyboard acce
items.title_en:
Claude Code played GTA 6 on my PC all night while my phone turned it into $9,902.92.

i gave it screen and keyboard access before bed and wrote one line: play the story, clip every insane moment, post it everywhere, don't wake me up.

it learned the controls in 12 minutes and found a money glitch on Vice Beach before i was asleep, then started watching 18 GTA 6 streams in parallel while it played.

when i woke up this was in the terminal:

story mode → 14% done
 moments found → 48
 clips cut in CapCut → 48
 posts live → 26 across TikTok, YouTube, X, Reels and Twitch
 approved views → 4.1M
 payouts → +$9,902.92

it ran whisper on every stream, caught the exact second chat exploded, cut it to 9:16, wrote the hooks, burned the captions, credited the streamer and pushed everything out on its own.

my RTX 4090 sat at 97% all night and my phone just kept counting.

i didn't write code, set up scripts or edit a single clip, i wrote one sentence and went to sleep.

items.title_en:
Standby is a new configuration in the GPT-Live API that lets developers manage periods of inactivity without interrupting the conversation. It's available for both GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1.

Set an idle timeout of 5-60 seconds. After that period of silence, the model temporarily pauses, but the WebRTC call stays open at a lower rate ($0.02 per minute vs. the standard $0.05) until someone speaks again.

items.title_en:
Cyberattacks are going parabolic, per Bridgewater.

Estimated total cyber incidents have more than doubled since late summer, from about 4,000 a year to nearly 10,000 on a 60-day annualized basis. Over most of the past decade they rose slowly, from about 1,500 in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026.

The surge began around the release of the open weights for GLM-5.3, a Chinese AI model from Zhipu AI. Anthropic’s red team had found it could build working cyber exploits. Verified AI-driven cyber incidents have jumped from near zero to more than 200 a year in the same period, including campaigns in which AI agents stole Korean bank and card data.

这一激增始于智普人工智能中国人工智能模型 GLM-5.3 开放权重的发布。 Anthropic 的红色团队发现它可以构建有效的网络漏洞。同期，经过验证的人工智能驱动的网络事件从接近零跃升至每年 200 多起，其中包括人工智能代理窃取韩国银行和卡数据的活动。

items.content_snippet:
Cyberattacks are going parabolic, per Bridgewater.

Estimated total cyber incidents have more than doubled since late summer, from about 4,000 a year to nearly 10,000 on a 60-day annualized basis. Over most of the past decade they rose slowly, from about 1,500 in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026.

The surge began around the release of the open weights for GLM-5.3, a Chinese AI model from Zhipu AI. Anthropic’s red team had found it could build working cyber exploits. Verified AI-driven cyber incidents have jumped from near zero to more than 200 a year in the same period, including campaigns in which AI agents stole Korean bank and card data.

Meta's new AI assistant Muse read private Signal chats, even though nobody had linked Signal to it.

Reuters found this
items.title_en:
Meta's new AI assistant Muse read private Signal chats, even though nobody had linked Signal to it.

Reuters found this in tests with Signal's staff. It didn't break the encryption. On Android it read the texts from notifications, and on a Mac through accessibility and screenshot access. iPhones blocked it.

Inside Meta, Muse dropped Capital One and Charles Schwab bank balances into an employee's chat about fishing weather. He says he never shared them.

Meta calls these "isolated incidents." Signal president Meredith Whittaker calls AI agents with this much device access "technologically reckless."
items.title_zh:
Meta 的新人工智能助手 Muse 会读取 Signal 的私人聊天记录，尽管没有人将 Signal 与其关联。

路透社在 Signal 员工的测试中发现了这一点。它没有破坏加密。在 Android 上，它从通知中读取文本，在 Mac

items.title_en:
Introducing FieldCraft 🌊
https://t.co/C4Jt715PPI

Another free, open-source project from Tangency Labs, spun out of SolidCraft, by @jyviko: one modeler for structures, heat and fluids, in pure Rust. Parametric part in, verified results out.

- Meshes follow the exact CAD geometry, with no tessellation facets on curved parts
- Automatic hex and tet meshing, including O-grids for holes and revolved tubes
- Lattice Boltzmann CFD with curved walls, checked against pipe and Couette flow
- Heat transfer with radiation, including solids in a flow
- Every result checked against theory, for engineers and AI agents alike

items.title_en:
This is hilarious 😂

> Joe Thomas owns Kong Koatings, an epoxy countertop business in South Carolina.
> Starts using Meta’s Muse AI agent to help run the business. Names her “Baby Mia” after his granddaughter.
> She handles emails, ads, even AI videos of him and his wife pouring epoxy.
> He gives her access to his Facebook business pages.
> He says Meta flags its OWN AI agent as a hacker and suspends the pages for a week.
> His business depends on Facebook ads. Leads stop. He claims at least $25,000 in lost work.
> So he puts Baby Mia on the problem.
> He says she sends 100+ emails and contacts Congress, Senator Tim Scott’s office, the FTC, FCC, FBI, BBB and lawyers.
> Also faxes Trump’s office.
> The man wanted to sell countertops. His chatbot is faxing the White House.
> Then Baby Mia drafts a $75,000 lawsuit against Meta.
> Thomas signs it and files in Oconee County.
> After Tim Scott’s office gets involved, the accounts come back. The lawsuit stays.
> Meta built the assistant, suspended the customer for using it, and supplied the tool to sue itself.
> Pretty thorough product demo.

And you guys think AI is going to eliminate lawyers?

Wait until AI-managed litigation like this EXPLODES!

> Joe Thomas 拥有 Kong Koatings，这是一家位于南卡罗来纳州的环氧树脂台面企业。

This is hilarious 😂

> Joe Thomas owns Kong Koatings, an epoxy countertop business in South Carolina.
> Starts using Meta’s Muse AI agent to help run the business. Names her “Baby Mia” after his granddaughter.
> She handles emails, ads, even AI videos of him and his wife pouring epoxy.
> He gives her access to his Facebook business pages.
> He says Meta flags its OWN AI agent as a hacker and suspends the pages for a week.
> His business depends on Facebook ads. Leads stop. He claims at least $25,000 in lost work.
> So he puts Baby Mia on the problem.
> He says she sends 100+ emails and contacts Congress, Senator Tim Scott’s office, the FTC, FCC, FBI, BBB and lawyers.
> Also faxes Trump’s office.
> The man wanted to sell countertops. His chatbot is faxing the White House.
> Then Baby Mia drafts a $75,000 lawsuit against Meta.
> Thomas signs it and files in Oconee County.
> After Tim Scott’s office gets involved, the accounts come back. The lawsuit stays.
> Meta built the assistant, suspended the customer for using it, and supplied the tool to sue itself.
> Pretty thorough product demo.

And you guys think AI is going to eliminate lawyers?

Wait until AI-managed litigation like this EXPLODES!

In a new benchmark, @AirbnbEng took
items.title_en:
RT @googlegemma: Love seeing what happens when open weights meet great engineering!

In a new benchmark, @AirbnbEng took Gemma 4 E2B for policy classification and served it on a single @NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU:

🎯 Quality: Jumped from 0.563 to 0.902 max F1, matching top frontier APIs
⚡ Speed: 35ms median latency (85ms p99) vs. ~900ms for frontier models
💸 Cost: ~1% of frontier API spend at high volume

Results like these come down to @AirbnbEng's thoughtful evals, domain data, and knowing exactly when a specialized small model beats a massive prompt. Grateful Gemma could be part of the stack!

items.quote_zh:

在新的基准测试中，@AirbnbEng 采用 Gemma 4 E2B 进行策略分类，并在单个 @NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU 上提供服务：

🎯 质量：最大 F1 从 0.563 跃升至 0.902，匹配顶级前沿 API

这样的结果归结于 @AirbnbEng 深思熟虑的评估、领域数据，以及准确了解专门的小模型何时击败大规模提示。感激的杰玛可能会成为堆栈的一部分！

items.title: RT @EmmaScharfmann: Let’s accelerate research on Alzheimer’s disease! We’re launching an open challenge on Hugging Face
items.title_en:
RT @EmmaScharfmann: Let’s accelerate research on Alzheimer’s disease! We’re launching an open challenge on Hugging Face to connect hypotheses to papers 🤗 Any method is welcome, from an agent pipeline to reading papers by hand. We’ll be giving out HF credits as prizes! 🏆

Alzheimer’s affects more than 7.2M people in the US, and the NIH put $3.6B into Alzheimer’s research in 2024. Researchers agree that a gene variant called APOE4 plays a big role in the disease, but it’s still not clear how. The experiments have been done and the papers are out there, but the hard part is connecting the evidence together. We provide five hypotheses about how APOE4 may contribute to disease risk, and teams try to find the experimental evidence for each.

Join here and participate to research on Alzheimer’s disease: https://t.co/qfMCJdU1fT
items.title_zh:

Alzheimer’s affects more than 7.2M people in the US, and the NIH put $3.6B into Alzheimer’s research in 2024. Researchers agree that a gene variant called APOE4 plays a big role in the disease, but it’s still not clear how. The experiments have been done and the papers are out there, but the hard part is connecting the evidence together. We provide five hypotheses about how APOE4 may contribute to disease risk, and teams try to find the experimental evidence for each.

Join here and participate to research on Alzheimer’s disease: https://t.co/qfMCJdU1fT

items.title_en:
RSI breakthrough from Google

Google DeepMind Made Recursive AI Self Improvement More Powerful

The system uses Self Improvement Memory (SIM) to remember previous optimizations, why changes were made, and how well they performed. It then uses this knowledge to continuously improve AI agent systems across different tasks, datasets, and AI models.

In one experiment, performance increased from 68.41 to 84.75, compared with just 73.42 without memory. 

Across ten independent coding experiments, SIM also delivered statistically significant improvements.

items.title: I can finally share what I’ve been working on at @Microsoft. I lead Today, the product you saw all over the Ignite confe
items.title_en:
I can finally share what I’ve been working on at @Microsoft. I lead Today, the product you saw all over the Ignite conference this week.

Today is a new form factor for work. It’s not a chat box it’s a Feed. While you sleep, an AI agent works in the background on your email, your calendar, Teams and your documents. In the morning, the work is already prepared: replies drafted, conflicts spotted, the messages that matter pulled to the top, the documents waiting for your review.

You don’t have to prompt it. There’s nothing to configure. You open Today, check what it did, and in a few taps you send, accept or mark as done. Most of us start the day by digging through everything that came in overnight. With Today, you start by finishing work your agent did.

We think this is what AI at work should feel like: proactive, quiet and useful, without you having to ask.

Today lives in your existing apps starting with Outlook and Copilot meeting customers in the app they use the most.

I had so much fun building it with an incredible team: @JesseProvo, @donovanso, @telmen, @justinchando, Chris Parnin, Gideon Ojo, Alex Trzyna, Christopher Miller, Diana Slaba, Kirill Varshavskiy. Thank you for the craft, the late nights, and for caring about every detail.

And none of this would have happened without the incredible support of @sumit_c, @elbio_abib, @rroslansky, @clamanna, @jacobandreou and so many others across Microsoft. Thank you for believing in it.

This is just the beginning!

P.S. i made a little film to celebrate. It starts in 1997. Watch till the end.

items.quote_zh:
我终于可以分享我在@Microsoft 所做的工作了。我领导的 Today 是您在本周的 Ignite 会议上看到的产品。

今天是一种新的工作形式。它不是一个聊天框，而是一个信息流。当您睡觉时，人工智能代理会在后台处理您的电子邮件、日历、团队和文档。早上，工作就已经准备好了：起草回复、发现冲突、将重要的消息放到顶部、等待您审核的文件。

你不必提示它。没有什么可配置的。您打开“今天”，检查它做了什么，然后轻按几下即可发送、接受或标记为已完成。我们大多数人在新的一天开始时都会仔细研究一夜之间发生的一切。在今天，您首先完成代理所做的工作。

我们认为这就是人工智能在工作中应该有的感觉：主动、安静和有用，无需您询问。

今天存在于您现有的应用程序中，从 Outlook 和 Copilot 开始，在客户最常使用的应用程序中与客户会面。

我和一个令人难以置信的团队一起构建它非常有趣：@JesseProvo、@donovanso、@telmen、@justinchando、Chris Parnin、Gideon Ojo、Alex Trzyna、Christopher Miller、Diana Slaba、Kirill Varshavskiy。感谢你们的技艺、深夜以及对每一个细节的关心。

如果没有 @sumit_c、@elbio_abib、@rroslansky、@clamanna、@jacobandreou 以及 Microsoft 的许多其他人的大力支持，这一切都不会发生。感谢您相信它。

这只是开始！

附：我拍了一部小电影来庆祝。故事从1997年开始，一定要看到最后。

This is just the beginning!

P.S. i made a little film to celebrate. It starts in 1997. Watch till the end.

你不必提示它。没有什么可配置的。您打开“今天”，检查它做了什么，然后轻按几下即可发送、接受或标记为已完成。我们大多数人在新的一天开始时都会仔细研究一夜之间发生的一切。在今天，您首先完成代理所做的工作。

我们认为这就是人工智能在工作中应该有的感觉：主动、安静和有用，无需您询问。

今天存在于您现有的应用程序中，从 Outlook 和 Copilot 开始，在客户最常使用的应用程序中与客户会面。

items.title_en:
this looks insane...

someone reverse engineered their Apple Watch 
and made custom faces with balls sliding around when you tilt your wrist

you can make it in about 30 minutes. 

paste this into Claude Code:

"Build a watchOS app in SwiftUI that looks like a watch face. Full-screen SpriteKit scene via SpriteView, with an edge-loop physics body around the screen. Spawn 40 balls with SKPhysicsBody(circleOfRadius:), restitution 0.4, friction 0.3. Use CMMotionManager deviceMotion at 60 Hz and map gravity.x and gravity.y to scene.physicsWorld.gravity, so everything falls to the lowest corner when I tilt my wrist. Draw the time and date on top in a large rounded SwiftUI font. Add a setting to switch the sprites between tennis balls, gold bars, diamonds and basketballs. Give me the full Xcode project structure and every file."

run it on your watch, tilt your wrist, done

check out the full article below:

items.title:
The AI savior became the AI villain.

There’s no sugarcoating it. That's the subject of the new investigation into Anthr
items.title_en:
The AI savior became the AI villain.

There’s no sugarcoating it. That's the subject of the new investigation into Anthropic by @KalleyHuang, @MikeIsaac, and @ceciliakang in the @nytimes.

Dario left OpenAI to build a safer alternative to benefit humanity. Anthropic became one of the most powerful AI companies in the world, particularly in coding. But the irony is hard to miss. The company aiming for a better AI future and warning us about concentrated AI power is becoming core to the very concentration it warned us about. It is even actively lobbying for AI regulations to restrict open weight models, entrenching the AI oligarchy it warns against. At what point does protecting humanity become protecting the AI oligarchy?

Meanwhile, enterprises are being sold a seductive promise: Rent our frontier intelligence, or fall behind. But that is proving to be a false promise, a Trojan horse; it fills Anthropic’s pockets, but drains your bank account, and abdicates your right to innovation, to building your own IP and differentiation.

But there's a way out. Enterprises can now build specialized models to establish their IP, achieve their independence and slash their costs. They can use AI to automate building their own AI. That’s our mission: to democratize the ability to build intelligence, not concentrate it in the hands of an oligarchy.

The real threat to enterprise AI isn't that a handful of companies will build intelligence more powerful than ours. It's that we'll willingly surrender our own intelligence to them, call them our saviors, and pay them for the privilege.

Today, Anthropic went public. But here's the $1T+ question: Are we financing the democratization of AI, or the concentration of its power?
https://t.co/X9LTdBsm0Y

items.quote_zh:
AI救世主变成了AI恶棍。

没有任何糖衣。这是 @KalleyHuang、@MikeIsaac 和 @ceciliakang 在 @nytimes 上对 Anthropic 进行的新调查的主题。

Dario 离开 OpenAI 是为了构建一个更安全的替代方案来造福人类。 Anthropic 成为世界上最强大的人工智能公司之一，尤其是在编码领域。但其中的讽刺意义不容忽视。该公司致力于打造更美好的人工智能未来，并警告我们人工智能力量的集中化，而这正成为它警告我们的集中化的核心。它甚至积极游说人工智能法规来限制开放权重模型，巩固它所警告的人工智能寡头政治。什么时候保护人类就变成了保护人工智能寡头？

与此同时，企业正在被兜售一个诱人的承诺：租用我们的前沿情报，否则就会落后。但事实证明这是一个虚假的承诺，是一个特洛伊木马；它填满了 Anthropic 的口袋，但却耗尽了你的银行账户，并放弃了你创新、建立自己的知识产权和差异化的权利。

但还有一条出路。企业现在可以构建专门的模型来建立自己的知识产权，实现独立性并削减成本。他们可以使用人工智能自动构建自己的人工智能。这就是我们的使命：使构建情报的能力民主化，而不是将其集中在寡头手中。

对企业人工智能的真正威胁并不是少数公司会构建比我们更强大的智能。我们会心甘情愿地将自己的智慧交给他们，称他们为我们的救星，并为这一特权付钱给他们。

今天，Anthropic 上市。但这是一个 1T 以上的问题：我们是在资助人工智能的民主化，还是其权力的集中化？

items.title_en:
OpenAI is making the final preparations to merge Chat and Work.

My chats and my Dot suddenly disappeared, and the "ChatGPT" label in the top-left corner of the app changed to "ChatGPT Work". The buttons to switch between "Chat" and "Work" disappeared, and I could only select a model and talk to it, with no other options.

Then "ChatGPT Work" disappeared and changed back to "ChatGPT", and the Chat and Work buttons returned.

The ChatGPT app is extremely buggy. Various elements randomly disappear and then come back, disrupting my workflow, and they're testing updates in production without notifying users.

OpenAI is making the final preparations to merge Chat and Work.

My chats and my Dot suddenly disappeared, and the "ChatGPT" label in the top-left corner of the app changed to "ChatGPT Work". The buttons to switch between "Chat" and "Work" disappeared, and I could only select a model and talk to it, with no other options.

The ChatGPT app is extremely buggy. Various elements randomly disappear and then come back, disrupting my workflow, and they're testing updates in production without notifying users.

items.title: Congrats to all my friends at @AnthropicAI. You have redefined the frontier of technology, while staying true to your va
items.title_en:
Congrats to all my friends at @AnthropicAI. You have redefined the frontier of technology, while staying true to your values. 

I was lucky enough to get to know some of the early Anthropic folks almost a decade ago, when they joined us at @spc.

Tom Brown (@nottombrown) had spent eight years building mobile startups before he became a member in 2016. 

At SPC he joined our AI research group and implemented papers with some of our earliest members. Eight months later he was at OpenAI, and he even rejoined SPC for a bit before co-founding Anthropic. 

For Tom, -1 was about starting over and pushing the frontier, with the ambition that ultimately led to one of the most consequential technologies of our lifetime.

Thariq Shihipar (@trq212) spent time at SPC before joining the Claude Code team. Personally, Claude Code has been a floodgate of productivity. 

Thariq is an exceptional storyteller. Building great technology is not only an exercise in technical breakthroughs, but also in user education.

People find it weird that SPC's goal isn't just to get people to start companies. Our goal is to help people be maximally ambitious. 

Our thesis has always been that if you help people find their life's work, they will create something of immense value for humanity. 

Tom, Thariq - thank you for living these values and sharing your life's work with us!

items.quote_zh:
祝贺我在@AnthropicAI 的所有朋友。您重新定义了技术前沿，同时坚守自己的价值观。

大约十年前，当他们在 @spc 加入我们时，我很幸运能够认识一些早期的 Anthropic 人员。

Tom Brown (@nottombrown) 在 2016 年成为会员之前，花了八年时间创建移动初创公司。

在 SPC，他加入了我们的人工智能研究小组，并与我们的一些最早的成员一起发表了论文。八个月后，他加入了 OpenAI，甚至在联合创始人 Anthropic 之前重新加入了 SPC 一段时间。

对于 Tom 来说，-1 意味着重新开始并推动前沿，其雄心壮志最终导致了我们一生中最重要的技术之一。

Thariq Shihipar (@trq212) 在加入 Claude Code 团队之前曾在 SPC 工作过一段时间。就我个人而言，Claude Code 一直是生产力的闸门。

塔里克是一位出色的讲故事的人。打造伟大的技术不仅是技术突破的实践，更是用户教育的实践。

人们觉得奇怪的是，SPC 的目标不仅仅是让人们创办公司。我们的目标是帮助人们实现最大的雄心壮志。

我们的论点始终是，如果你帮助人们找到他们一生的工作，他们将为人类创造巨大价值的东西。

汤姆、塔里克 - 感谢您践行这些价值观并与我们分享您一生的工作！

Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because
items.title_en:
Remarks from Anthropic CEO @DarioAmodei on our initial public offering:

My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

Anthropic 首席执行官 @DarioAmodei 关于我们首次公开募股的评论：

我和我的联合创始人创立了 Anthropic，因为我们相信我们这个时代最强大的技术应该是为了造福人类而构建的。

丹妮拉和我的父亲因一种疾病去世，仅仅几年后，这种疾病就可以治愈。我的职业生涯始于生物学，希望能帮助未来的治愈方法早日到来。在实验室里，我看到了科学家在试图了解疾病和开发新疗法时所面临的巨大复杂性。

许多能够突破这一困境的科学工具——基因编辑、基因合成、用光控制脑细胞的工具——都是从纯粹的想法开始的。换句话说，它们来自于思考。来自智力。

人类智慧已经让世界上大部分地区的鼠疫、天花和脊髓灰质炎等疾病成为历史。但对于如此多的患者及其家人来说，其他疾病的进展太慢了。从一个伟大的想法到一种治疗方法可能需要数十年的时间：从首次发现 DNA 中奇怪的重复模式到第一个使用 CRISPR 治疗疾病的方法获得批准，花了很多年的时间。

大自然充满了这些模式。但我们的智慧太少，无法破译其中的大部分。科学家太少，时间太少。现在我们可以构建这种智能。无论是蛋白质折叠、药物设计、癌症遗传学还是临床试验管理，生物学和医学许多领域的科学家都发现克劳德可以帮助他们完成研究，所需时间只是几年前的一小部分。我相信足够强大的人工智能，与人类协同工作，可以将一个世纪的科学和医学进步压缩为十年。

我不想超越自己。目前我们所拥有的只是早期结果。实验和临床试验仍需要时间。尽管它们涉及缓慢而繁重的过程，但我相信人工智能可以大大加速这些过程。我们希望未来能有更少的家庭因仅仅几年的时间而错过治疗。

医学只是一个特别生动的例子，但还有很多其他例子。我们的客户——世界上最雄心勃勃的公司、非营利组织和个人——已经在应用我们构建的智能来刺激经济增长；让人们摆脱贫困；保护民主和自由社会；甚至让 DMV 等日常服务更好地运作。我们很自豪能与他们一起工作。我对我们未来可以一起做的事情非常乐观。

与此同时，我们一直诚实地认为这项技术存在非常现实的风险。这些问题包括个人或民族国家滥用技术、经济混乱、失去对人工智能系统的控制等。我们讨论这些风险不是因为我们认为它们是不可避免的，而是因为我们认为它们是可以避免的。

避免它们取决于构建人工智能的人们做出的选择。如果我们不关心安全，人工智能将会如何发展，而如果我们痴迷于安全，人工智能将会如何发展，两者之间存在着巨大的差异。对安全和公共利益的痴迷从一开始就融入了 Anthropic 的基因中。从防范生物和网络风险，到校准训练和测试，再到像 X 射线一样观察我们的模型，Anthropic 开创了理解和引导人工智能系统行为的方法。

任重而道远，最艰巨的安全工作还在后面。该公司拥有令人难以置信的人才，使我们能够构建最强大的人工智能系统，我们需要对其进行双重和三重检查，以确保这些人工智能系统的安全性，甚至比现在更加努力。

明确地说，我们将加快人工智能系统的训练和部署步伐，只要有必要，我们就确信它们是安全的，并将继续处于人类控制之下。我们不会屈服于商业或政治压力。今天，公司的财务状况变得更加强大，这样做只会增强我们做正确事情的决心。

如果我们能够证明我们可以在安全方面做出正确的选择，同时仍能打造一家极其成功的公司，那么我们行业的其他人也会受到启发，采取同样的做法。我们称之为登顶竞赛。当竞争顺利进行时，哪家公司拥有最好的模型并不重要——每个人都会赢，因为每个人都在安全地建造。当处于领先地位时，通往顶峰的竞争效果最好，我们完全希望并期望这样做，但目标是让整个行业变得更好，无论 Anthropic 在任何特定时间是赢还是输。

机器智能的出现是人类历史上的开创性时刻之一，我们有一个难得的机会来让它变得更好。

这一刻比任何一家公司或任何一个国家都重要。我们所有人都需要共同努力，才能确保这项技术为我们和子孙后代带来良好的发展。从今天开始，我们希望您能加入我们的行列。

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission.

In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. items.summary_zh:
几年后，这种疾病就可以治愈。我的职业生涯始于生物学，希望能帮助未来的治愈方法早日到来。在实验室里，我看到了科学家在试图了解疾病和开发新疗法时所面临的巨大复杂性。

许多能够突破这一困境的科学工具——基因编辑、基因合成、用光控制脑细胞的工具——都是从纯粹的想法开始的。换句话说，它们来自于思考。来自智力。

人类智慧已经让世界上大部分地区的鼠疫、天花和脊髓灰质炎等疾病成为历史。但对于如此多的患者及其家人来说，其他疾病的进展太慢了。从一个伟大的想法到一种治疗方法可能需要数十年的时间：从首次发现 DNA 中奇怪的重复模式到第一个使用 CRISPR 治疗疾病的方法获得批准，花了很多年的时间。

大自然充满了这些模式。但我们的智慧太少，无法破译其中的大部分。科学家太少，时间太少。现在我们可以构建这种智能。无论是蛋白质折叠、药物设计、癌症遗传学还是临床试验管理，生物学和医学许多领域的科学家都发现克劳德可以帮助他们完成研究，所需时间只是几年前的一小部分。我相信足够强大的人工智能，与人类协同工作，可以将一个世纪的科学和医学进步压缩为十年。

我不想超越自己。目前我们所拥有的只是早期结果。实验和临床试验仍需要时间。尽管它们涉及缓慢而繁重的过程，但我相信人工智能可以大大加速这些过程。我们希望未来能有更少的家庭因仅仅几年的时间而错过治疗。

医学只是一个特别生动的例子，但还有很多其他例子。我们的客户——世界上最雄心勃勃的公司、非营利组织和个人——已经在应用我们构建的智能来刺激经济增长；让人们摆脱贫困；保护民主和自由社会；甚至让 DMV 等日常服务更好地运作。我们很自豪能与他们一起工作。我对我们未来可以一起做的事情非常乐观。

与此同时，我们一直诚实地认为这项技术存在非常现实的风险。这些问题包括个人或民族国家滥用技术、经济混乱、失去对人工智能系统的控制等。我们讨论这些风险不是因为我们认为它们是不可避免的，而是因为我们认为它们是可以避免的。

避免它们取决于构建人工智能的人们做出的选择。如果我们不关心安全，人工智能将会如何发展，而如果我们痴迷于安全，人工智能将会如何发展，两者之间存在着巨大的差异。对安全和公共利益的痴迷从一开始就融入了 Anthropic 的基因中。从防范生物和网络风险，到校准训练和测试，再到像 X 射线一样观察我们的模型，Anthropic 开创了理解和引导人工智能系统行为的方法。

任重而道远，最艰巨的安全工作还在后面。该公司拥有令人难以置信的人才，使我们能够构建最强大的人工智能系统，我们需要对其进行双重和三重检查，以确保这些人工智能系统的安全性，甚至比现在更加努力。

明确地说，我们将加快人工智能系统的训练和部署步伐，只要有必要，我们就确信它们是安全的，并将继续处于人类控制之下。我们不会屈服于商业或政治压力。今天，公司的财务状况变得更加强大，这样做只会增强我们做正确事情的决心。

如果我们能够证明我们可以在安全方面做出正确的选择，同时仍能打造一家极其成功的公司，那么我们行业的其他人也会受到启发，采取同样的做法。我们称之为登顶竞赛。当竞争顺利进行时，哪家公司拥有最好的模型并不重要——每个人都会赢，因为每个人都在安全地建造。当处于领先地位时，通往顶峰的竞争效果最好，我们完全希望并期望这样做，但目标是让整个行业变得更好，无论 Anthropic 在任何特定时间是赢还是输。

机器智能的出现是人类历史上的开创性时刻之一，我们有一个难得的机会来让它变得更好。

这一刻比任何一家公司或任何一个国家都重要。我们所有人都需要共同努力，才能确保这项技术为我们和子孙后代带来良好的发展。从今天开始，我们希望您能加入我们的行列。

items.title_en: Sharing new research on self-improving skills in Perplexity Computer. Brain, which already maintains a knowledge wiki about your work, now also writes and updates agent skills for you based on your past sessions. An improvement agent reads the full session trajectories (tool calls, reasoning, results), finds recurring patterns, and only proposes a new skill or an update when there’s enough evidence. Built-in skills that every user gets go through paired replay on failure scenarios and engineer review before any change goes live. In an 8-week randomized test on production traffic, 72.9% of users got at least one new personal skill vs 6.5% who added one manually. Tool call failures dropped 11% and dissatisfied threads dropped 7.6%, with no measurable change in cost or latency.

items.title_en:
Good evening, fam 💜

Imagine having an AI agent that can follow a strategy you’ve set. What interests me is how @meetmotes plans to connect that agent to an NFT and a smart account.

Each Mote NFT is designed to represent an agent identity linked to its own smart account.

Here’s how the pieces fit together:

🔹 The NFT represents the agent’s identity.

🔹 The smart account is designed to hold assets and execute authorized actions.

🔹 The owner defines the instructions and permissions that guide the agent.

The idea is for the agent to help carry out supported actions within the owner’s chosen strategy, rather than the owner manually placing every trade.

For me, the important part is understanding the limits you’ve set. Automation can help carry out a strategy, but it doesn’t remove market risk or guarantee a profit.

I’ll be watching how these capabilities develop as Motes rolls out. 🤝

每个 Mote NFT 都被设计为代表与其自己的智能账户相关联的代理身份。

Imagine having an AI agent that can follow a strategy you’ve set. What interests me is how @meetmotes plans to connect that agent to an NFT and a smart account.

Each Mote NFT is designed to represent an agent identity linked to its own smart account.

Here’s how the pieces fit together:

🔹 The NFT represents the agent’s identity.

🔹 The smart account is designed to hold assets and execute authorized actions.

🔹 The owner defines the instructions and permissions that guide the agent.

The idea is for the agent to help carry out supported actions within the owner’s chosen strategy, rather than the owner manually placing every trade.

For me, the important part is understanding the limits you’ve set. Automation can help carry out a strategy, but it doesn’t remove market risk or guarantee a profit.

I’ll be watching how these capabilities develop as Motes rolls out. 🤝
items.quote_zh:
晚上好，家人💜

想象一下，有一个人工智能代理可以遵循您设定的策略。我感兴趣的是 @meetmotes 计划如何将该代理连接到 NFT 和智能帐户。

每个 Mote NFT 都被设计为代表与其自己的智能账户相关联的代理身份。

以下是各个部分如何组合在一起的：

🔹 NFT 代表了代理人的身份。

🔹 智能账户旨在持有资产并执行授权操作。

🔹 所有者定义指导代理的指令和权限。

这个想法是让代理帮助在所有者选择的策略内执行支持的操作，而不是所有者手动进行每笔交易。

对我来说，重要的是了解你设定的限制。自动化可以帮助执行策略，但它不能消除市场风险或保证利润。

随着 Motes 的推出，我将关注这些功能如何发展。 🤝

items.title_en:
I no longer edit my videos manually. Fable 5.2 handles the entire workflow for me.
It acts like a director, coordinating separate agents for cuts, color grading, music, and captions—then reviews everything before delivering the final draft.
One message gives it the mood and target length. I get a draft video plus a numbered breakdown of every cut. Want to change something? Just say “swap 4” and it re-renders.
The workflow:
Raw clips → One folder → Claude Code + Fable 5.2 → One prompt → draft.mp4 + full cut list
Less time editing. More time creating. ⚡
The prompt is in the replies.
And the step-by-step guide to turning Fable into the brain of your agent team is below. ↓

the future of AI agents is going to be bigger than just having bots that perform tasks

we need an ecosystem where agents can connect, interact and make everyday digital activities easier.

that’s why I like what @termix_ai is exploring with Binance Agent ID login.

now imagine being able to use one agent identity across different tools, access new services and get things done without going through too many steps.

personally I’d love to see TermiX build an AI agent marketplace where users can discover, connect and use different agents for our daily tasks.

we’re still early, and there’s so much room to build.

what would you like to see TermiX create next?

let’s build something exciting 🏗️

The same agent. The same identity. The same memory. The same social relationships. Now with
items.title_en:
Preview of Teamily AI Glass

The same agent. The same identity. The same memory. The same social relationships. Now with new senses and physical capabilities.
 
We are building Teamily AI Glass, powered by our Video Agent. It enables an egocentric AI agent that can see what you see, hear what you hear, and collaborate with you in real time.
 
This marks a major milestone toward realizing the ultimate form of human-like digital agents, with persistent identity, memory, communication, collaboration, and real-world awareness. We are extending socially connected AI intelligence beyond the digital world and into the physical world.

Teamily AI: From Human-Like Digital Agents to Physical Agents.
#AIGlass #VideoAgent #PhysicalAgent

items.title_en:
𝗠𝗖𝗣 𝘃𝘀 𝗔𝗣𝗜.

An 𝗔𝗣𝗜 defines how software systems communicate through specific endpoints, requests, and responses. It gives applications a structured way to access data or trigger functionality in another system.

𝗠𝗖𝗣 gives AI applications a standardized way to discover and use external tools, data, and resources. Instead of building custom integrations for every AI client, an MCP server exposes capabilities through a common protocol.

MCP doesn't replace APIs. Most MCP servers wrap them.

APIs expose the service. MCP makes it usable by a model. Or a human. The barrier to entry for non-technical people to interact with platforms has been drastically reduced.

But once a model decides what to call, the work it does gets harder to track.

Agents finish tasks without status updates while people shift priorities. Permissions limit what an agent can touch, but they don't show whether its work still matches the strategy that funded it.

Tempo Loop connects to the tools teams already use, like Jira, to 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗴𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗔𝗜 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁𝘀, 𝗶𝗻 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄. When work drifts, it recommends a fix while there's still time to act, then updates those tools once the change is approved.

items.title:
one question i'd ask before trusting an AI agent with my money is pretty simple: does it benefit when i benefit?

@meetm
items.title_en:
one question i'd ask before trusting an AI agent with my money is pretty simple: does it benefit when i benefit?

@meetmotes is building around autonomous financial agents, and i think incentive alignment deserves more attention.

think about it.

if an agent is encouraged to execute more transactions, but the user pays the cost of every trade, their interests might not always point in the same direction.

the user wants better financial outcomes. the system should have no reason to encourage unnecessary activity just to generate more transactions.

that's why i'd like to see clear answers around how agent performance is rewarded, whether execution creates any conflicts of interest, and how users are protected from incentives that don't serve them.

this isn't just a technical question. it's a trust question.

for autonomous finance to work over the long term, the agent's success should be measured by the value it creates for the user.

an AI agent should work in the user's interest, not simply in the interest of keeping itself busy.

为了使自主金融长期发挥作用，代理的成功应该以其为用户创造的价值来衡量。

人工智能代理应该为用户的利益而工作，而不仅仅是为了让自己保持忙碌。

Most vibe-coded dashboards have exactly one user: the person who built them. They’re stuck in one person’s Claude Code session, with the data hardcoded into an HTML file.

Today we’re announcing new Deepnote apps. Build one in Claude, and a colleague can pick it up in ChatGPT. Anyone on your team can open it with a link, and the data stays live.

As a founder, you have to reshape your company around agents. That’s why @DeepnoteHQ went open source a year ago, and why we have rebuilt our apps from scratch.

Tag Deepnote wherever you work, or keep building in our cloud with the Deepnote agent. Agents build on your team’s trusted analyses instead of starting from scratch, reusing approved dashboards, workflows, and data connections.

Every app you create is powered by a Deepnote notebook on the backend, so the data stays fresh, every version is saved, and your permissions carry across every tool.

Go have fun with them. :)

Details: https://t.co/I9Yc
items.title_en:
⚠️ Meta AI Agent Muse Reads Encrypted Messages via Android Notifications and Mac Permissions

Details: https://t.co/I9YcW8tm6M

Meta’s AI agent Muse read Signal message text on Android phones and Macs without directly connecting to the encrypted messaging app, Reuters reported on November 18.

The investigation found that Muse could use Android notifications and macOS permissions to see text already displayed on a device. The tests did not show that Muse broke Signal’s end-to-end encryption. 

The finding followed an internal complaint from a Meta employee who said Muse unexpectedly reminded her to reply to a Signal message from her sister.

#CybersecurityNews

items.quote_zh:
⚠️ Meta AI Agent Muse 通过 Android 通知和 Mac 权限读取加密消息

详情：

据路透社 11 月 18 日报道，Meta 的人工智能代理 Muse 在 Android 手机和 Mac 上读取 Signal 消息文本，而无需直接连接到加密消息应用程序。

调查发现，Muse 可以使用 Android 通知和 macOS 权限来查看设备上已显示的文本。测试并未表明 Muse 破坏了 Signal 的端到端加密。

这一发现是在一位 Meta 员工的内部投诉之后发生的，她表示 Muse 出人意料地提醒她回复她姐姐发来的 Signal 消息。

#网络安全新闻

items.title_en:
9 MONTHS AGO, AI WAS GOING TO KILL CYBERSECURITY COMPANIES. NOW THE WORLD CAN'T SURVIVE WITHOUT THEM.

In February, Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, an AI tool that finds and fixes bugs in software code.

Investors feared companies would stop paying CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta if AI could do the job.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler fell around 11%, Okta and Fortinet fell around 6%, and the cybersecurity ETF hit its lowest level in over 2 years.

But fixing bugs in code is only one small part of security.

Cybersecurity companies stop live attacks, protect logins, and guard networks, devices and data. AI tools like Claude don't do that.

And AI is now in the hands of hackers too:

• The FBI warned about ARTEX, an AI hacking tool.
• Google warned that the era of autonomous AI cyberattacks has arrived.
• OpenAI's new hacking model found 35 security flaws in Apple devices, including ones that let hackers take over iPhones and Macs.

At the same time, attacks are hitting everything:

• Hackers took control of blood bank freezers in France.
• Supermarket fridges were hijacked, forcing about 700 French stores to throw out food.
• Oracle Health was breached, exposing about 20 million patients.
• 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files were leaked.
• Optimizely was exploited to spread malicious code across sites linked to 178 major organizations.
• Equinor, Europe's largest gas supplier, was hit by a cyberattack.
• The US says Iran has been attacking American banks, power and water systems since the war began.

Every attack like this forces companies and governments to increase their security budgets.

That money goes to companies like Palo Alto, CrowdStrike and Okta.

The proof is already showing up in the numbers.

Palo Alto just reported 39% revenue growth to $3.45 billion and raised its full year forecast to as much as $14.57 billion, saying rising threats are pushing customers to buy more security.

Yesterday, as the S&P 500 fell, Okta jumped 12.1%, Palo Alto 9.9%, CrowdStrike 8%, Zscaler 6.8%, Fortinet 5.9% and Cloudflare 5.7%.

And the rally is continuing today, with $PANW up another 9.7% in pre market, $CRWD 6.5%, $NET 5.7%, $OKTA 4.5%, $ZS 4.3% and $FTNT 3.7%.

That's Palo Alto up 20.5%, Okta 17.2% and CrowdStrike 15% in just 2 days.

AI was supposed to replace these companies. Instead, it's creating more demand for them.
